# About this document

This document holds the whole Study 2 quantitative pipeline of the Surfwell realist evaluation (University of Exeter) in one place, in the order it runs: cleaning, merging, recoding, scoring, descriptive tables, the measure lookup, statistical analysis, figures and a package citation record. Each stage passes its result to the next through files in the project's `data/` folder, so every stage can be re-run on its own once the stage before it has been run.

## The stages and their files

| Stage | What it does | Reads | Writes |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 1 | Cleans the raw Qualtrics exports | `data/raw/tp1_final.xlsx`, `tp4_final.xlsx`, `tp5_final.xlsx` | `data/clean/cleaned_tp1.rds`, `cleaned_tp4.rds`, `cleaned_tp5.rds` |
| 2 | Renames columns and merges the timepoints | `cleaned_tp*.rds` | `data/clean/merged_data.rds`, `program_theory.xlsx` |
| 3 | Recodes text responses to numbers | `merged_data.rds` | `data/clean/recoded_data.rds` |
| 4a | Scores each measure | `recoded_data.rds` | `data/clean/scored_data.rds` |
| 4b | Builds attrition, participant characteristics and mental health summary tables | `scored_data.rds`, `cleaned_tp*.rds` | `data/analysis/participant_characteristics_TP1_TP4_TP5.xlsx` |
| 4c | Records how each measure is grouped and labelled | nothing | `data/analysis/measure_groups.rdata` |
| 5 | Descriptives, tests, Bonferroni correction and RCI | `scored_data.rds`, `measure_groups.rdata` | `data/analysis/analysis_results.rdata`, `test_results_summary.xlsx` |
| 6 | Bar charts and RCI scatter plots | `analysis_results.rdata`, `measure_groups.rdata` | figures in `data/analysis/` |
| 7 | Programme theory bar chart | `data/clean/program_theory.xlsx` | figure in `data/analysis/` |
| 8 | RCI stacked-bar figures | `analysis_results.rdata`, `measure_groups.rdata` | figures in `data/analysis/` |
| 9 | Package citations and session record | this document (as text) | `data/analysis/pipeline_citations.bib`, `pipeline_sessionInfo.txt` |

Stage 4c sits before stage 5 because stage 5 loads `measure_groups.rdata`. Stage 7 needs only stage 2's output, so it can run at any point after stage 2. Stage 9 reads this document's own code, so run it last, in the same R session as the other stages.

## Running it

1.  Open the R project for the study, so that `here::here()` resolves paths from the project root. All file paths in this document are relative to that root.
2.  Put the three raw exports in `data/raw/`.
3.  Run the stages in the order above. Each stage starts with a Setup chunk that loads the packages it needs.
4.  **Stage 5 is interactive.** It pauses for a y/n answer after the outlier checks and after the test recommendations, and it has a step where you edit an Excel file before continuing. Run stage 5 chunk by chunk from the console. The interactive prompts stop with an error when the document is rendered unattended, so the document cannot be rendered from top to bottom in one go.
5.  Stages 6 to 8 read the files stage 5 saves, so they can be re-run without repeating the analysis.

## Creating an R script from this document

To extract the code as a plain R script, run this in the R console:

``` r
knitr::purl("surfwell_study2_pipeline.qmd",
            output = "surfwell_study2_pipeline.R",
            documentation = 2)
```

`documentation = 2` keeps the explanatory text as comments above the code it describes, so the script reads in the same order as this document. Chunk options (the `#|` lines) are kept as comments. The script inherits the same interactive behaviour in stage 5, so run it in sections and not with `source()`.

## Conventions used throughout

- Timepoints are TP1 (1-Week Before), TP4 (2-Week Follow-Up) and TP5 (3-Month Follow-Up).
- Chunk labels carry the stage as a prefix (for example `s05-setup`), because labels must be unique within one document.
- Stage 4c is the single source for measure groups, display order, titles and axis labels, so tables and figures agree.

# Stage 1: Data cleaning

## How this stage runs

**Reads:** the three raw Qualtrics Excel exports in `data/raw/` (`tp1_final.xlsx`, `tp4_final.xlsx`, `tp5_final.xlsx`).

**Writes:** `data/clean/cleaned_tp1.rds`, `cleaned_tp4.rds` and `cleaned_tp5.rds`.

What it does:

1.  Loads the raw TP1, TP4 and TP5 files.
2.  Removes irrelevant metadata columns. Column positions differ per timepoint, because each survey had a different set of embedded and system columns.
3.  Removes the extra header row Qualtrics adds under the real column names. It repeats the question text and is not data.
4.  Saves each cleaned timepoint for stage 2.

### Setup

```{r}
#| label: s01-setup
#| message: false

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(here)
```

### Load raw data

```{r}
#| label: s01-load-data
tp1 <- read_excel(here("data", "raw", "tp1_final.xlsx"))
tp4 <- read_excel(here("data", "raw", "tp4_final.xlsx"))
tp5 <- read_excel(here("data", "raw", "tp5_final.xlsx"))
```

### Remove irrelevant columns and the Qualtrics header row

Each timepoint's Qualtrics export has a different set of metadata/system columns to drop (timestamps, IP addresses, embedded data fields, etc.), which is why the column positions differ below. After dropping those, we remove row 1 from each dataset — this is a second header row Qualtrics adds that repeats the full question text, not real data.

```{r}
#| label: s01-remove-columns-and-header-row
# TP1: drop columns 1-17 and 114-118, then remove header row
tp1 <- tp1[, -c(1:17, 114:118)]
tp1 <- tp1[-1, ]

# TP4: drop columns 1-17 and 79-96, then remove header row
tp4 <- tp4[, -c(1:17, 79:96)]
tp4 <- tp4[-1, ]

# TP5: drop columns 1-17 and 108-112, then remove header row
tp5 <- tp5[, -c(1:17, 108:112)]
tp5 <- tp5[-1, ]
```

### Save cleaned data

```{r}
#| label: s01-save-cleaned-data
if (!dir.exists(here("data", "clean"))) {
  dir.create(here("data", "clean"), recursive = TRUE)
}

saveRDS(tp1, here("data", "clean", "cleaned_tp1.rds"))
saveRDS(tp4, here("data", "clean", "cleaned_tp4.rds"))
saveRDS(tp5, here("data", "clean", "cleaned_tp5.rds"))
```

# Stage 2: Rename columns and merge

## How this stage runs

**Reads:** `data/clean/cleaned_tp1.rds`, `cleaned_tp4.rds`, `cleaned_tp5.rds`.

**Writes:** `data/clean/merged_data.rds` (all three timepoints, one row per participant) and `data/clean/program_theory.xlsx` (the Programme Theory questions).

What it does:

1.  Renames each `Q1` column to `ID` and converts it to a whole number, so the three timepoints can be merged on a common key.
2.  Checks for duplicate IDs within each timepoint.
3.  Renames the raw `Q`-coded columns in each timepoint to meaningful names (for example `Q7_1` becomes `SWEMWBS_1_TP1`). Each rename is one column to one name, and a check chunk precedes each timepoint's rename block.
4.  Merges the three timepoints by `ID` with full outer joins, so nobody is dropped for missing a timepoint at this stage.
5.  Pulls the Programme Theory questions out into their own file.
6.  Folds "Other" free-text responses into their matching choice column, then drops the free-text column.
7.  Saves the merged data and the Programme Theory data.

### Setup

```{r}
#| label: s02-setup
#| message: false

library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(writexl)
library(here)
```

### Load cleaned data

```{r}
#| label: s02-load-data
tp1 <- readRDS(here("data", "clean", "cleaned_tp1.rds"))
tp4 <- readRDS(here("data", "clean", "cleaned_tp4.rds"))
tp5 <- readRDS(here("data", "clean", "cleaned_tp5.rds"))
```

### Rename ID column and convert to integer

Each timepoint's participant ID currently lives in a column called `Q1`. We check it exists, rename it to `ID`, then convert it to a whole number so all three timepoints use the same ID format for merging.

```{r}
#| label: s02-check-id-column-exists
if (!"Q1" %in% names(tp1)) {
  stop("TP1 does not have a column named Q1. Cannot rename to ID.")
}
if (!"Q1" %in% names(tp4)) {
  stop("TP4 does not have a column named Q1. Cannot rename to ID.")
}
if (!"Q1" %in% names(tp5)) {
  stop("TP5 does not have a column named Q1. Cannot rename to ID.")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: s02-rename-and-convert-id
tp1 <- tp1 |> rename(ID = Q1)
tp4 <- tp4 |> rename(ID = Q1)
tp5 <- tp5 |> rename(ID = Q1)

tp1$ID <- as.integer(as.character(tp1$ID))
tp4$ID <- as.integer(as.character(tp4$ID))
tp5$ID <- as.integer(as.character(tp5$ID))
```

### Check for duplicate IDs

A duplicate ID within a single timepoint is a problem for the merge step: `full_join()` matches *every* row with a given ID against *every* row with that ID in the other timepoints, so a duplicate can silently multiply a participant's rows without you noticing.

```{r}
#| label: s02-check-duplicate-ids
dup_tp1 <- tp1$ID[duplicated(tp1$ID)]
dup_tp4 <- tp4$ID[duplicated(tp4$ID)]
dup_tp5 <- tp5$ID[duplicated(tp5$ID)]

if (length(dup_tp1) > 0) {
  cat("⚠️ Duplicate ID(s) in TP1:", paste(unique(dup_tp1), collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
if (length(dup_tp4) > 0) {
  cat("⚠️ Duplicate ID(s) in TP4:", paste(unique(dup_tp4), collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
if (length(dup_tp5) > 0) {
  cat("⚠️ Duplicate ID(s) in TP5:", paste(unique(dup_tp5), collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
if (length(dup_tp1) == 0 && length(dup_tp4) == 0 && length(dup_tp5) == 0) {
  cat("✅ No duplicate IDs found in any timepoint.\n")
}

cat("\nTP1:", length(unique(tp1$ID)), "unique IDs (", nrow(tp1), "rows )\n")
cat("TP4:", length(unique(tp4$ID)), "unique IDs (", nrow(tp4), "rows )\n")
cat("TP5:", length(unique(tp5$ID)), "unique IDs (", nrow(tp5), "rows )\n")
```

### Rename TP1 columns

Renames the raw `Q`-coded columns to meaningful measure names (e.g. `SWEMWBS_1_TP1`, `BAT_12_TP1`). The check below confirms every expected raw column is present before renaming — if the raw file's columns don't match what's expected, this stops with a clear error rather than silently renaming the wrong things.

```{r}
#| label: s02-check-tp1-columns
expected_tp1 <- c(
  "Q2", "Q3", "Q4", "Q4_5_TEXT", "Q5", "Q6", "Q6_5_TEXT",
  paste0("Q7_", 1:7),
  paste0("Q8_", 1:8),
  paste0("Q9_", 1:7),
  paste0("Q10_", 1:6),
  paste0("Q11_", 1:3),
  paste0("Q12_", 1:6),
  paste0("Q13_", 1:3),
  "Q14", "Q15", "Q16", "Q17", "Q18", "Q19a", "Q19b", "Q19c", "Q19d", "Q19e",
  "Q20", "Q21", "Q22", "Q23_1", "Q23_2", "Q23_3", "Q23_4", "Q23_5", "Q23_6",
  "Q24_1", "Q24_2", "Q24_3",
  paste0("Q25_", 1:6),
  paste0("Q26_", 1:12),
  "Q27", "Q28", "Q29", "Q30", "Q31", "Q32", "Q33", "Q34"
)
missing_tp1 <- setdiff(expected_tp1, names(tp1))
if (length(missing_tp1) > 0) {
  stop("TP1 is missing these columns before renaming:\n  ",
       paste(missing_tp1, collapse = ", "))
}
```

### Merge TP1, TP4 and TP5

Full outer joins on `ID`: any participant present in TP1 or TP4 or TP5 is kept. If they weren't present at a given timepoint, that timepoint's columns become `NA` for them — nobody is dropped at this stage.

```{r}
#| label: s02-merge-timepoints
m14 <- tp1 |> full_join(tp4, by = join_by(ID))
message("After merging TP1+TP4: ", nrow(m14), " rows x ", ncol(m14), " columns")

merged_data <- m14 |> full_join(tp5, by = join_by(ID))
message("After merging TP1+TP4+TP5: ", nrow(merged_data), " rows x ", ncol(merged_data), " columns")
```

### Extract Programme Theory questions

Pulls out any column starting with `ProgTheory_` into its own data frame, then removes those columns from `merged_data`.

```{r}
#| label: s02-extract-programme-theory
prog_columns <- grep("^ProgTheory_", names(merged_data), value = TRUE)

if (length(prog_columns) == 0) {
  message("No ProgTheory_ columns found. Skipping extraction.")
  program_theory_df <- tibble(ID = merged_data$ID)
} else {
  message("Programme Theory columns extracted: ", paste(prog_columns, collapse = ", "))
  program_theory_df <- merged_data |> select(ID, all_of(prog_columns))
  merged_data <- merged_data |> select(-all_of(prog_columns))
}
```

### Fold "Other" free-text responses into their choice column

Some questions have a multiple-choice column (e.g. `Service_choice1_TP1`) paired with a free-text column for when the participant selects "Other" (e.g. `Service_other2_TP1`). This step replaces "Other" in the choice column with whatever the participant actually typed, then drops the now-redundant free-text column.

```{r}
#| label: s02-fold-other-text
other_cols <- grep("_other2_TP\\d+$", names(merged_data), value = TRUE)

if (length(other_cols) == 0) {
  message("No _other2_TP... columns found. Skipping 'Other' consolidation.")
} else {
  message("Will process these 'other' columns: ", paste(other_cols, collapse = ", "))
  for (other_col in other_cols) {
    choice_col <- sub("_other2_", "_choice1_", other_col)
    if (!choice_col %in% names(merged_data)) {
      warning("Could not find matching choice column for '", other_col, "'. Skipping.")
      next
    }
    rows_to_fix <- which(merged_data[[choice_col]] == "Other")
    if (length(rows_to_fix) > 0) {
      message("  - Replacing 'Other' in '", choice_col, "' for ", length(rows_to_fix),
              " row(s) using text from '", other_col, "'")
      merged_data[[choice_col]][rows_to_fix] <- merged_data[[other_col]][rows_to_fix]
    }
  }
  merged_data <- merged_data |> select(-all_of(other_cols))
  message("Dropped columns: ", paste(other_cols, collapse = ", "))
}
```

```{r}
}
```

# Stage 3: Recode responses

## How this stage runs

**Reads:** `data/clean/merged_data.rds`.

**Writes:** `data/clean/recoded_data.rds`.

This stage converts every measure's text response options (for example `"quite a bit"`, `"strongly agree"`) into the numeric values needed for scoring in stage 4a. Each of the 13 measures follows the same pattern:

1.  Capture the pre-recode values, so there is something to compare against.
2.  Recode the values with `case_when()` logic specific to that measure's response options.
3.  Check that no values silently became `NA` that were not `NA` before. If any did, the pipeline stops and shows exactly which rows and values changed, so a mismatched label cannot slip through unnoticed.

### Setup

```{r}
#| label: s03-setup
#| message: false

library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(here)
```

### Load merged data

```{r}
#| label: s03-load-data
merged_data <- readRDS(here("data", "clean", "merged_data.rds"))

# Recoding into a new object name so the original merged data is always
# still available to compare back against if needed
recoded_data <- merged_data
```

### The NA-tracking function

Recoding relies on matching each raw text response (e.g. `"quite a bit"`) to the exact string it expects. If a response in your data doesn't match any of the expected strings — a typo, an unexpected wording, a blank — `case_when()` silently turns it into `NA` rather than raising an error. That's dangerous here, because it can look identical to a value that was already missing.

`track_new_na()` guards against this. It compares a set of columns before and after recoding, counts anything that went from "had a value" to `NA`, and if it finds any:

- builds a small table showing exactly which rows and which old values triggered it, saved to your environment as `<measure_name>_new_na_df`
- stops the whole script with an error naming the affected columns, so you have to look at it before continuing

If nothing unexpected happened, it prints a confirmation message and you're safe to move to the next measure.

```{r}
#| label: s03-define-track-new-na
track_new_na <- function(df_before, df_after, cols, measure_name) {
  new_na_counts <- sapply(cols, function(col) {
    before_na <- is.na(df_before[[col]])
    after_na  <- is.na(df_after[[col]])
    sum(after_na & !before_na)
  })

  if (any(new_na_counts > 0)) {
    old_subset <- df_before[, cols, drop = FALSE]
    new_subset <- df_after[, cols, drop = FALSE]

    new_na_mat <- is.na(new_subset) & !is.na(old_subset)
    rows_with_new_na <- which(rowSums(new_na_mat) > 0)

    old_vals <- old_subset[rows_with_new_na, , drop = FALSE]
    new_vals <- new_subset[rows_with_new_na, , drop = FALSE]

    names(old_vals) <- paste0(names(old_vals), "_old")
    names(new_vals) <- paste0(names(new_vals), "_new")

    review_df <- cbind(
      row_number = rows_with_new_na,
      old_vals,
      new_vals
    )

    assign(
      paste0(measure_name, "_new_na_df"),
      review_df,
      envir = .GlobalEnv
    )

    stop(
      "Recode introduced NAs in ", measure_name,
      " column(s): ",
      paste(names(new_na_counts[new_na_counts > 0]), collapse = ", ")
    )
  }

  empty_old <- df_before[FALSE, , drop = FALSE]
  empty_new <- df_after[FALSE, cols, drop = FALSE]

  names(empty_old) <- paste0(names(empty_old), "_old")
  names(empty_new) <- paste0(names(empty_new), "_new")

  empty_review <- cbind(
    row_number = integer(0),
    empty_old,
    empty_new
  )

  assign(
    paste0(measure_name, "_new_na_df"),
    empty_review,
    envir = .GlobalEnv
  )

  message("No new NA's from recoding ", measure_name, ", you are safe to continue")
}
```

### Demographics: Age and Gender

`Age_TP1` is binned into four groups. `Gender_TP1` is mapped to a factor with an explicit level order (`male`, `female`, `other`); "prefer not to say" is treated as missing rather than as its own category.

```{r}
#| label: s03-recode-demographics
old_demographics <- recoded_data |> select(Age_TP1, Gender_TP1)

recoded_data <- recoded_data |>
  mutate(
    Age_bin = case_when(
      Age_TP1 < 30                 ~ "<30",
      Age_TP1 >= 30 & Age_TP1 < 40 ~ "30–39",
      Age_TP1 >= 40 & Age_TP1 < 50 ~ "40–49",
      Age_TP1 >= 50                ~ "50+",
      TRUE                         ~ NA_character_
    ),
    Gender_f = case_when(
      tolower(trimws(Gender_TP1)) == "male"                      ~ "male",
      tolower(trimws(Gender_TP1)) == "female"                    ~ "female",
      tolower(trimws(Gender_TP1)) == "non-binary / other gender" ~ "other",
      tolower(trimws(Gender_TP1)) == "prefer not to say"         ~ NA_character_,
      TRUE                                                       ~ NA_character_
    ) |> factor(levels = c("male", "female", "other"))
  )

track_new_na(old_demographics, recoded_data, c("Age_TP1", "Gender_TP1"), "DEMOGRAPHICS")
```

```{r}
    trimws(tolower(as.character(.))) == "none of the time"  ~ 1,
    trimws(tolower(as.character(.))) == "rarely"             ~ 2,
    trimws(tolower(as.character(.))) == "some of the time"   ~ 3,
    trimws(tolower(as.character(.))) == "often"               ~ 4,
    trimws(tolower(as.character(.))) == "all of the time"    ~ 5,
    !is.na(as.numeric(.))                                     ~ as.numeric(.),
    TRUE                                                      ~ NA_real_
  ))))

track_new_na(old_swemwbs, recoded_data, swemwbs_columns, "SWEMWBS")
```

### MHSIS

MHSIS mixes three different question formats across its three items (likelihood, true/false, agreement), which is why the "strip trailing anchor label" step runs first — e.g. `"Extremely unlikely - 1"` becomes `"extremely unlikely"` before matching.

```{r}
#| label: s03-recode-mhsis
old_mhsis <- recoded_data |> select(all_of(mhsis_columns))

recoded_data <- recoded_data |>
  mutate(across(all_of(mhsis_columns), ~ sub("\\s*-\\s*[0-9]+$", "", as.character(.)))) |>
  mutate(across(all_of(mhsis_columns), ~ suppressWarnings(case_when(
    tolower(trimws(.)) == "extremely unlikely"  ~ 1,
    tolower(trimws(.)) == "extremely likely"    ~ 7,
    tolower(trimws(.)) == "definitely false"    ~ 1,
    tolower(trimws(.)) == "definitely true"     ~ 7,
    tolower(trimws(.)) == "strongly disagree"   ~ 1,
    tolower(trimws(.)) == "strongly agree"      ~ 7,
    !is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.)))     ~ as.numeric(.),
    TRUE                                        ~ NA_real_
  ))))

track_new_na(old_mhsis, recoded_data, mhsis_columns, "MHSIS")
```

# Stage 4a: Scoring

## How this stage runs

**Reads:** `data/clean/recoded_data.rds`.

**Writes:** `data/clean/scored_data.rds`.

This stage computes subscale and total scores, severity bands and categories for each measure, following each instrument's own scoring guidance:

- **SWEMWBS:** raw sum converted to a metric score via a lookup table, then categorised.
- **PHQ-8:** total score, severity band, probable-depression flag.
- **GAD-7:** total score, severity band, probable-GAD flag.
- **ITQ:** PTSD and DSO symptom totals, cluster endorsements, CPTSD category (Cloitre et al., 2018).
- **MHSIS:** mean score.
- **HPQ:** absenteeism (hours not worked, per the Kessler et al., 2003/2004 scoring memo) and presenteeism (absolute presenteeism score), reported as two separate figures with no combined "hours lost" metric. TP1 and TP5 only, because HPQ is not administered at TP4 (see `project-context/references/measures.md`).
- **BRS:** mean score.
- **UWES:** summed score.
- **OSES:** summed score.
- **BAT-12:** four subscale means plus an overall mean (TP1, TP4, TP5).
- **GSPA:** weighted total and activity category (Godin & Shephard, 2011).
- **INTL:** summed total.

Each measure gets its own small `*_results` data frame (ID plus that measure's scored columns) for interactive checking. These are not saved to disk individually. Only the full `scored_data` is saved, at the end.

### Setup

```{r}
#| label: s04a-setup
#| message: false

library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(readr)
library(here)
```

### Load recoded data

```{r}
#| label: s04a-load-data
scored_data <- readRDS(here("data", "clean", "recoded_data.rds"))
```

### SWEMWBS scoring

Raw sum scores (range 7–35) are converted to SWEMWBS's official "metric" score via a fixed lookup table, then grouped into Low/Average/High bands based on ±1 SD around the population mean (mean = 23.5, SD = 3.9 → cut-points at 19.5 and 27.5).

```{r}
#| label: s04a-swemwbs-conversion-table
swemwbs_conv <- tibble(
  raw    = 7:35,
  metric = c(7.00,  9.51, 11.25, 12.40, 13.33, 14.08, 14.75,
             15.32, 15.84, 16.36, 16.88, 17.43, 17.98, 18.59,
             19.25, 19.98, 20.73, 21.54, 22.35, 23.21, 24.11,
             25.03, 26.02, 27.03, 28.13, 29.31, 30.70, 32.55,
             35.00)
)

swemwbs_columns_TP1 <- grep("^SWEMWBS_.*TP1$", names(scored_data), value = TRUE)
swemwbs_columns_TP4 <- grep("^SWEMWBS_.*TP4$", names(scored_data), value = TRUE)
swemwbs_columns_TP5 <- grep("^SWEMWBS_.*TP5$", names(scored_data), value = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: s04a-swemwbs-scoring
scored_data <- scored_data |>
  mutate(
    SWEMWBS_Raw_TP1 = rowSums(pick(all_of(swemwbs_columns_TP1))),
    SWEMWBS_Raw_TP4 = rowSums(pick(all_of(swemwbs_columns_TP4))),
    SWEMWBS_Raw_TP5 = rowSums(pick(all_of(swemwbs_columns_TP5)))
  ) |>
  left_join(swemwbs_conv, by = join_by(SWEMWBS_Raw_TP1 == raw)) |>
  rename(SWEMWBS_Metric_TP1 = metric) |>
  left_join(swemwbs_conv, by = join_by(SWEMWBS_Raw_TP4 == raw)) |>
  rename(SWEMWBS_Metric_TP4 = metric) |>
  left_join(swemwbs_conv, by = join_by(SWEMWBS_Raw_TP5 == raw)) |>
  rename(SWEMWBS_Metric_TP5 = metric) |>
  mutate(
    SWEMWBS_Cat_TP1 = case_when(
      SWEMWBS_Metric_TP1 < 19.5                              ~ "Low",
      SWEMWBS_Metric_TP1 >= 19.5 & SWEMWBS_Metric_TP1 < 27.5  ~ "Average",
      SWEMWBS_Metric_TP1 >= 27.5                              ~ "High",
      TRUE                                                    ~ NA_character_
    ),
    SWEMWBS_Cat_TP4 = case_when(
      SWEMWBS_Metric_TP4 < 19.5                              ~ "Low",
      SWEMWBS_Metric_TP4 >= 19.5 & SWEMWBS_Metric_TP4 < 27.5  ~ "Average",
      SWEMWBS_Metric_TP4 >= 27.5                              ~ "High",
      TRUE                                                    ~ NA_character_
    ),
    SWEMWBS_Cat_TP5 = case_when(
      SWEMWBS_Metric_TP5 < 19.5                              ~ "Low",
      SWEMWBS_Metric_TP5 >= 19.5 & SWEMWBS_Metric_TP5 < 27.5  ~ "Average",
      SWEMWBS_Metric_TP5 >= 27.5                              ~ "High",
      TRUE                                                    ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
```

### PHQ-8 scoring

Total score (0–24), five-band severity (based on PHQ-8 scoring instructions), and a probable-depression flag at the ≥10 cut-off (Kroenke et al., 2009 — prevalence of depression was similar whether defined by the diagnostic algorithm or a PHQ-8 score ≥10).

```{r}
#| label: s04a-phq8-scoring
phq8_TP1 <- grep("^PHQ8_.*TP1$", names(scored_data), value = TRUE)
phq8_TP4 <- grep("^PHQ8_.*TP4$", names(scored_data), value = TRUE)
phq8_TP5 <- grep("^PHQ8_.*TP5$", names(scored_data), value = TRUE)

scored_data <- scored_data |>
  mutate(
    PHQ8_Total_TP1 = rowSums(pick(all_of(phq8_TP1))),
    PHQ8_Total_TP4 = rowSums(pick(all_of(phq8_TP4))),
    PHQ8_Total_TP5 = rowSums(pick(all_of(phq8_TP5))),

    PHQ8_Severity_TP1 = case_when(
      PHQ8_Total_TP1 >= 20 ~ "severe",
      PHQ8_Total_TP1 >= 15 ~ "moderately severe",
      PHQ8_Total_TP1 >= 10 ~ "moderate",
      PHQ8_Total_TP1 >= 5  ~ "mild",
      PHQ8_Total_TP1 >= 0  ~ "minimal",
      TRUE                 ~ NA_character_
    ),
    PHQ8_Severity_TP4 = case_when(
      PHQ8_Total_TP4 >= 20 ~ "severe",
      PHQ8_Total_TP4 >= 15 ~ "moderately severe",
      PHQ8_Total_TP4 >= 10 ~ "moderate",
      PHQ8_Total_TP4 >= 5  ~ "mild",
      PHQ8_Total_TP4 >= 0  ~ "minimal",
      TRUE                 ~ NA_character_
    ),
    PHQ8_Severity_TP5 = case_when(
      PHQ8_Total_TP5 >= 20 ~ "severe",
      PHQ8_Total_TP5 >= 15 ~ "moderately severe",
      PHQ8_Total_TP5 >= 10 ~ "moderate",
      PHQ8_Total_TP5 >= 5  ~ "mild",
      PHQ8_Total_TP5 >= 0  ~ "minimal",
      TRUE                 ~ NA_character_
    ),

    PHQ8_ProbableDepression_TP1 = case_when(
      PHQ8_Total_TP1 >= 10 ~ "probable depression",
      PHQ8_Total_TP1 < 10  ~ "no depression",
      TRUE                 ~ NA_character_
    ),
    PHQ8_ProbableDepression_TP4 = case_when(
      PHQ8_Total_TP4 >= 10 ~ "probable depression",
      PHQ8_Total_TP4 < 10  ~ "no depression",
      TRUE                 ~ NA_character_
    ),
    PHQ8_ProbableDepression_TP5 = case_when(
      PHQ8_Total_TP5 >= 10 ~ "probable depression",
      PHQ8_Total_TP5 < 10  ~ "no depression",
      TRUE                 ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
```

```{r}
      GAD7_Total_TP5 >= 5  ~ "mild",

    GAD7_ProbableGAD_TP1 = case_when(

      TRUE                ~ NA_character_
    ),

    ),
    GAD7_ProbableGAD_TP5 = case_when(

    )
  )
```

### ITQ scoring

Based on the ITQ manual and Cloitre et al. (2018). PTSD symptom total (P1–P6), Disturbances in Self-Organization (DSO) total (C1–C6), and combined CPTSD total. Each symptom cluster is "endorsed" if either of its two items scores ≥2; a diagnostic criterion is met only if all its clusters are endorsed. `ITQ_Category` combines the PTSD and DSO criteria into "CPTSD" / "PTSD" / "None". TP1 and TP5 only, per the assessment schedule.

```{r}
#| label: s04a-itq-scoring
scored_data <- scored_data |>
  mutate(
    # Symptom totals (P1-P6 and C1-C6 kept separate; impairment items P7-P9/C7-C9 excluded from totals)
    ITQ_PTSD_Total_TP1  = rowSums(pick(ITQ_P1_TP1:ITQ_P6_TP1)),
    ITQ_DSO_Total_TP1   = rowSums(pick(ITQ_C1_TP1:ITQ_C6_TP1)),
    ITQ_CPTSD_Total_TP1 = ITQ_PTSD_Total_TP1 + ITQ_DSO_Total_TP1,

    ITQ_PTSD_Total_TP5  = rowSums(pick(ITQ_P1_TP5:ITQ_P6_TP5)),
    ITQ_DSO_Total_TP5   = rowSums(pick(ITQ_C1_TP5:ITQ_C6_TP5)),
    ITQ_CPTSD_Total_TP5 = ITQ_PTSD_Total_TP5 + ITQ_DSO_Total_TP5,

    # Cluster endorsements (TRUE/FALSE, cut-off >= 2 on either item in the pair)
    ITQ_RE_TP1       = (ITQ_P1_TP1 >= 2) | (ITQ_P2_TP1 >= 2),
    ITQ_AV_TP1       = (ITQ_P3_TP1 >= 2) | (ITQ_P4_TP1 >= 2),
    ITQ_TH_TP1       = (ITQ_P5_TP1 >= 2) | (ITQ_P6_TP1 >= 2),
    ITQ_PTSDFI_TP1   = (ITQ_P7_TP1 >= 2) | (ITQ_P8_TP1 >= 2) | (ITQ_P9_TP1 >= 2),
    ITQ_PTSDCrit_TP1 = ITQ_RE_TP1 & ITQ_AV_TP1 & ITQ_TH_TP1 & ITQ_PTSDFI_TP1,

    ITQ_AD_TP1       = (ITQ_C1_TP1 >= 2) | (ITQ_C2_TP1 >= 2),
    ITQ_NSC_TP1      = (ITQ_C3_TP1 >= 2) | (ITQ_C4_TP1 >= 2),
    ITQ_DR_TP1       = (ITQ_C5_TP1 >= 2) | (ITQ_C6_TP1 >= 2),
    ITQ_DSOFI_TP1    = (ITQ_C7_TP1 >= 2) | (ITQ_C8_TP1 >= 2) | (ITQ_C9_TP1 >= 2),
    ITQ_DSOCrit_TP1  = ITQ_AD_TP1 & ITQ_NSC_TP1 & ITQ_DR_TP1 & ITQ_DSOFI_TP1,

    ITQ_Category_TP1 = case_when(
      ITQ_PTSDCrit_TP1 == TRUE & ITQ_DSOCrit_TP1 == TRUE ~ "CPTSD",
      ITQ_PTSDCrit_TP1 == TRUE                            ~ "PTSD",
      ITQ_PTSDCrit_TP1 == FALSE                           ~ "None",
      TRUE                                                 ~ NA_character_
    ),
    ITQ_ProbablePTSD_TP1  = if_else(ITQ_PTSDCrit_TP1 & !ITQ_DSOCrit_TP1, "yes", "no"),
    ITQ_ProbableCPTSD_TP1 = if_else(ITQ_PTSDCrit_TP1 & ITQ_DSOCrit_TP1, "yes", "no"),

    # Repeat for TP5
    ITQ_RE_TP5       = (ITQ_P1_TP5 >= 2) | (ITQ_P2_TP5 >= 2),
    ITQ_AV_TP5       = (ITQ_P3_TP5 >= 2) | (ITQ_P4_TP5 >= 2),
    ITQ_TH_TP5       = (ITQ_P5_TP5 >= 2) | (ITQ_P6_TP5 >= 2),
    ITQ_PTSDFI_TP5   = (ITQ_P7_TP5 >= 2) | (ITQ_P8_TP5 >= 2) | (ITQ_P9_TP5 >= 2),
    ITQ_PTSDCrit_TP5 = ITQ_RE_TP5 & ITQ_AV_TP5 & ITQ_TH_TP5 & ITQ_PTSDFI_TP5,

    ITQ_AD_TP5       = (ITQ_C1_TP5 >= 2) | (ITQ_C2_TP5 >= 2),
    ITQ_NSC_TP5      = (ITQ_C3_TP5 >= 2) | (ITQ_C4_TP5 >= 2),
    ITQ_DR_TP5       = (ITQ_C5_TP5 >= 2) | (ITQ_C6_TP5 >= 2),
    ITQ_DSOFI_TP5    = (ITQ_C7_TP5 >= 2) | (ITQ_C8_TP5 >= 2) | (ITQ_C9_TP5 >= 2),
    ITQ_DSOCrit_TP5  = ITQ_AD_TP5 & ITQ_NSC_TP5 & ITQ_DR_TP5 & ITQ_DSOFI_TP5,

    ITQ_Category_TP5 = case_when(
      ITQ_PTSDCrit_TP5 == TRUE & ITQ_DSOCrit_TP5 == TRUE ~ "CPTSD",
      ITQ_PTSDCrit_TP5 == TRUE                            ~ "PTSD",
      ITQ_PTSDCrit_TP5 == FALSE                           ~ "None",
      TRUE                                                 ~ NA_character_
    ),
    ITQ_ProbablePTSD_TP5  = if_else(ITQ_PTSDCrit_TP5 & !ITQ_DSOCrit_TP5, "yes", "no"),
    ITQ_ProbableCPTSD_TP5 = if_else(ITQ_PTSDCrit_TP5 & ITQ_DSOCrit_TP5, "yes", "no")
  )

ITQ_results <- scored_data |>
  select(
    ID,
    starts_with("ITQ_PTSD_Total"), starts_with("ITQ_DSO_Total"), starts_with("ITQ_CPTSD_Total"),
    starts_with("ITQ_RE_"), starts_with("ITQ_AV_"), starts_with("ITQ_TH_"), starts_with("ITQ_PTSDFI_"),
    starts_with("ITQ_PTSDCrit_"), starts_with("ITQ_AD_"), starts_with("ITQ_NSC_"), starts_with("ITQ_DR_"),
    starts_with("ITQ_DSOFI_"), starts_with("ITQ_DSOCrit_"), starts_with("ITQ_Category"),
    starts_with("ITQ_ProbablePTSD"), starts_with("ITQ_ProbableCPTSD")
  )
```

### HPQ scoring

Reports two separate figures, following Kessler et al.'s official HPQ absenteeism/presenteeism scoring memo (2003/2004). TP1 and TP5 only — HPQ wasn't administered at TP4 (its past-month reference period doesn't fit a 2-week follow-up window; see `measures.md`).

**Absenteeism** — `HPQ_absenteeism_hours_4w`: hours not worked in the past 4 weeks. Prefers the 4-week direct estimate (`4×B4 − B6`) when `B6` is present, and falls back to the 7-day estimate scaled up to 4 weeks (`4×B4 − 4×B3`) when it isn't — exactly as the memo specifies.

**Presenteeism** — `HPQ_presenteeism_percent`: `10×B11`, the memo's "absolute presenteeism scoring rule".

```{r}
#| label: s04a-hpq-scoring
scored_data <- scored_data |>
  mutate(
    ## Absenteeism (TP1) — hours not worked in the past 4 weeks
    HPQ_absenteeism_4w_TP1       = (4 * HPQ_B4_TP1) - HPQ_B6_TP1,
    HPQ_absenteeism_7d_TP1       = (4 * HPQ_B4_TP1) - (4 * HPQ_B3_TP1),
    HPQ_absenteeism_hours_4w_TP1 = case_when(
      !is.na(HPQ_B6_TP1) ~ HPQ_absenteeism_4w_TP1,
      !is.na(HPQ_B3_TP1) ~ HPQ_absenteeism_7d_TP1,
      TRUE               ~ NA_real_
    ),
    HPQ_absenteeism_days_4w_TP1  = round(HPQ_absenteeism_hours_4w_TP1 / (HPQ_B4_TP1 / 7), 1),

    ## Presenteeism (TP1) — absolute presenteeism score (Kessler et al., 2003)
    HPQ_presenteeism_percent_TP1  = 10 * HPQ_B11_TP1,

    ## Absenteeism (TP5)
    HPQ_absenteeism_4w_TP5       = (4 * HPQ_B4_TP5) - HPQ_B6_TP5,
    HPQ_absenteeism_7d_TP5       = (4 * HPQ_B4_TP5) - (4 * HPQ_B3_TP5),
    HPQ_absenteeism_hours_4w_TP5 = case_when(
      !is.na(HPQ_B6_TP5) ~ HPQ_absenteeism_4w_TP5,
      !is.na(HPQ_B3_TP5) ~ HPQ_absenteeism_7d_TP5,
      TRUE               ~ NA_real_
    ),
    HPQ_absenteeism_days_4w_TP5  = round(HPQ_absenteeism_hours_4w_TP5 / (HPQ_B4_TP5 / 7), 1),

    ## Presenteeism (TP5)
    HPQ_presenteeism_percent_TP5  = 10 * HPQ_B11_TP5
  )

HPQ_results <- scored_data |>
  select(ID, starts_with("HPQ_absenteeism"), starts_with("HPQ_presenteeism"))
```

### BAT-12 scoring

Four subscale means (Exhaustion: items 1–3; Mental Distance: 4–6; Emotional Impairment: 7–9; Cognitive Impairment: 10–12) plus an overall 12-item mean, computed for all three timepoints in a loop.

```{r}
#| label: s04a-bat-scoring
timepoints <- c("TP1", "TP4", "TP5")

for (tp in timepoints) {
  exhaustion_cols      <- paste0("BAT_", 1:3,  "_", tp)
  mental_distance_cols <- paste0("BAT_", 4:6,  "_", tp)
  emo_imp_cols         <- paste0("BAT_", 7:9,  "_", tp)
  cog_imp_cols         <- paste0("BAT_", 10:12, "_", tp)
  all_items_cols       <- paste0("BAT_", 1:12, "_", tp)

  scored_data <- scored_data |>
    mutate(
      "BAT_Exhaustion_{tp}"      := round(rowMeans(pick(all_of(exhaustion_cols)), na.rm = FALSE), 1),
      "BAT_MentalDistance_{tp}"  := round(rowMeans(pick(all_of(mental_distance_cols)), na.rm = FALSE), 1),
      "BAT_EmoImpairment_{tp}"   := round(rowMeans(pick(all_of(emo_imp_cols)), na.rm = FALSE), 1),
      "BAT_CogImpairment_{tp}"   := round(rowMeans(pick(all_of(cog_imp_cols)), na.rm = FALSE), 1),
      "BAT_TotalMean_{tp}"       := round(rowMeans(pick(all_of(all_items_cols)), na.rm = FALSE), 1)
    )
}

BAT_results <- scored_data |>
  select(
    ID,
    starts_with("BAT_Exhaustion_"), starts_with("BAT_MentalDistance_"),
    starts_with("BAT_EmoImpairment_"), starts_with("BAT_CogImpairment_"), starts_with("BAT_TotalMean_")
  )
```

### GSPA (Godin-Shepard) scoring

Weighted total following Godin & Shephard (2011): 9 × strenuous + 5 × moderate + 3 × mild exercise sessions per week. Categorised as Active (≥24), Moderately active (14–23), or Insufficiently active (\<14).

```{r}
#| label: s04a-gspa-scoring
timepoints <- c("TP1", "TP4", "TP5")

for (tp in timepoints) {
  strenuous <- paste0("GSPA_1_", tp)
  moderate  <- paste0("GSPA_2_", tp)
  mild      <- paste0("GSPA_3_", tp)

  scored_data <- scored_data |>
    mutate(
      "GSPA_Total_{tp}" := (9 * .data[[strenuous]]) + (5 * .data[[moderate]]) + (3 * .data[[mild]]),
      "GSPA_Category_{tp}" := case_when(
        .data[[paste0("GSPA_Total_", tp)]] >= 24 ~ "Active",
        .data[[paste0("GSPA_Total_", tp)]] >= 14 ~ "Moderately active",
        .data[[paste0("GSPA_Total_", tp)]] < 14  ~ "Insufficiently active",
        TRUE                                     ~ NA_character_
      )
    )
}

GSPA_results <- scored_data |>
  select(ID, starts_with("GSPA_Total_"), starts_with("GSPA_Category_"))
```

```{r}
}

write_rds(scored_data, here("data", "clean", "scored_data.rds"))

message("Saved: data/clean/scored_data.rds")
```

# Stage 4b: Participant characteristics

## How this stage runs

**Reads:** `data/clean/scored_data.rds`, and the cleaned per-timepoint files `data/clean/cleaned_tp1.rds`, `cleaned_tp4.rds`, `cleaned_tp5.rds` (for the attrition counts only).

**Writes:** `data/analysis/participant_characteristics_TP1_TP4_TP5.xlsx`.

This stage produces descriptive manuscript tables. It does not feed the statistical analysis in stage 5 and does not change `recoded_data.rds` or `scored_data.rds`.

1.  **Attrition / retention table:** how many people responded at each of TP1, TP4 and TP5, and what percentage of the baseline sample that represents.
2.  **Participant characteristics table:** age (continuous and banded), gender, emergency service, occupation, and number of Surfwell sessions previously attended, all at baseline (TP1).
3.  **Mental health summary table:** proportion of the baseline (TP1) sample meeting each diagnostic or banding cutoff: SWEMWBS wellbeing band, probable depression (PHQ-8), probable GAD (GAD-7), probable PTSD (ITQ) and probable CPTSD (ITQ).
4.  Exports all three tables to a single `.xlsx` workbook for pasting into the manuscript.

::: callout-warning
**Two choices differ from the conventions used in stage 5.**

1.  **Gender uses the raw `Gender_TP1` text and not the recoded `Gender_f`.** Stage 3 treats "prefer not to say" as missing (`NA`) in `Gender_f`, which suits a 3-level analysis factor. In a participant characteristics table "prefer not to say" is a real, reportable response, and collapsing it into "missing" would understate how many people were asked and chose not to answer, so it is kept as its own category. To match stage 5, swap `Gender_TP1` for `Gender_f` in the chunk below.
2.  **Occupation (`Jobtitle_TP1`) and Surfwell sessions previously attended (`SurfwellSession_choice1_TP1`) are reported as raw frequency tables, with no manual collapsing.** `Jobtitle_TP1` is free text, so the table may hold a long list of near-duplicate entries (for example different phrasings of the same role). Check it manually before it goes in the manuscript.
:::

::: callout-note
**Attrition means raw survey completion, and not "complete cases" in the stage 5 sense.** Stage 5's complete-case filter asks whether a person has a valid score on a specific measure at all three timepoints. The attrition table asks whether the person responded to the TP1, TP4 or TP5 survey at all. The two numbers will differ, because someone can complete the TP4 survey but skip an item needed for a particular measure's score. To avoid confusing "did not do this survey" with "skipped one item", the attrition counts read the raw ID list for each timepoint from stage 1's output, before merging.
:::

::: callout-note
**Run order.** Attrition, participant characteristics and the mental health summary all read from `scored_data.rds`, so stage 4a must have been run since the last change to stages 1 to 3. Otherwise this stage errors or runs on stale data.
:::

### Setup

```{r}
#| label: s04b-setup
#| message: false

library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(writexl)
library(here)
```

### Attrition / retention

```{r}
#| label: s04b-get-raw-timepoint-ids
# Pulls unique participant IDs directly from each timepoint's cleaned (but
# not-yet-merged) data. Q1 is still the raw ID column here — it isn't renamed
# to `ID` until stage 2. as.integer(as.character(.)) is
# used because Q1 may be read in as a factor-like or character column; going
# via as.character() first avoids the classic R trap where as.integer() on a
# factor returns the factor's internal level numbers, not the ID value itself.
get_unique_ids <- function(path) {
  readRDS(path) |>
    mutate(ID = as.integer(as.character(Q1))) |>
    pull(ID) |>
    unique() |>
    (\(x) x[!is.na(x)])()
}

tp1_ids <- get_unique_ids(here("data", "clean", "cleaned_tp1.rds"))
tp4_ids <- get_unique_ids(here("data", "clean", "cleaned_tp4.rds"))
tp5_ids <- get_unique_ids(here("data", "clean", "cleaned_tp5.rds"))
```

```{r}
#| label: s04b-attrition-table
attrition_table <- tibble(
  Timepoint = c("Baseline (TP1)", "2-Week Follow-Up (TP4)", "3-Month Follow-Up (TP5)"),
  N         = c(length(tp1_ids), length(tp4_ids), length(tp5_ids))
) |>
  mutate(Percent_Retained = round(100 * N / N[1], 1))

print(attrition_table)
```

### Load scored data for participant characteristics

Uses `scored_data.rds` as the single data source for this stage, so the demographics table and the mental health table cannot disagree about who is in the sample. The demographic columns are not touched by scoring (they pass through stage 4a unchanged from `recoded_data`), and `scored_data` additionally holds the diagnostic and banding columns needed for the mental health summary table below.

```{r}
#| label: s04b-load-scored-data
scored_data <- readRDS(here("data", "clean", "scored_data.rds"))
```

Restricts to people who actually completed the TP1 (baseline) survey. `scored_data` is built from the full outer-joined dataset from stage 2 (via `recoded_data`), so it can contain rows for people who only appear at TP4 or TP5 — their TP1 demographic columns would just be `NA`, which would otherwise silently count as "missing" in the table below rather than "never asked."

```{r}
#| label: s04b-restrict-to-baseline-sample
baseline_data <- scored_data |> filter(ID %in% tp1_ids)

message("Participant characteristics table based on N = ", nrow(baseline_data), " baseline (TP1) respondents.")
```

### Participant characteristics table

```{r}
#| label: s04b-define-categorical-summary-helper
# Turns one categorical column into a tidy Variable / Category / N / Percent
# table. NA values are shown as their own "Missing" row rather than being
# dropped, so the denominator is always visible.
summarise_categorical <- function(data, var, var_label) {
  data |>
    mutate(Category = coalesce(as.character(.data[[var]]), "Missing")) |>
    count(Category, name = "N") |>
    mutate(
      Variable = var_label,
      Percent  = round(100 * N / sum(N), 1)
    ) |>
    select(Variable, Category, N, Percent)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: s04b-age-continuous
# Age_TP1 is never explicitly converted to numeric anywhere upstream (01-04)
# — it's renamed from Q2 at stage 2 and used in text comparisons at
# stage 3, but its actual type depends on whatever readxl/Qualtrics exported.
# mean()/sd() don't error on a non-numeric column, they silently return NA
# with a warning, which is what was happening here. Converting explicitly,
# with the same before/after NA guard used elsewhere in this pipeline (see
# stage 3's track_new_na()) so a genuine bad value doesn't just vanish.
age_before  <- baseline_data$Age_TP1
age_numeric <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(age_before)))

age_new_na <- sum(is.na(age_numeric) & !is.na(age_before))
if (age_new_na > 0) {
  warning(
    age_new_na, " value(s) in Age_TP1 could not be converted to a number ",
    "and are now NA (were not NA before conversion). This is likely a ",
    "non-numeric entry in the raw data (e.g. a typo or stray text) rather ",
    "than a true missing response. Check: ",
    "baseline_data$ID[is.na(age_numeric) & !is.na(age_before)]"
  )
}

age_continuous <- tibble(
  Variable  = "Age (years)",
  N         = sum(!is.na(age_numeric)),
  Mean      = round(mean(age_numeric, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
  SD        = round(sd(age_numeric, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
  Min       = min(age_numeric, na.rm = TRUE),
  Max       = max(age_numeric, na.rm = TRUE),
  N_Missing = sum(is.na(age_numeric))
)

print(age_continuous)
```

```{r}
#| label: s04b-categorical-demographics
demographics_categorical <- bind_rows(
  summarise_categorical(baseline_data, "Age_bin", "Age group"),
  summarise_categorical(baseline_data, "Gender_TP1", "Gender"),
  summarise_categorical(baseline_data, "Service_choice1_TP1", "Emergency service"),
  summarise_categorical(baseline_data, "Jobtitle_TP1", "Occupation"),
  summarise_categorical(baseline_data, "SurfwellSession_choice1_TP1", "Surfwell sessions previously attended")
)

print(demographics_categorical)
```

### Mental health summary table (TP1)

Reuses `baseline_data` (loaded above) and `summarise_categorical()` (defined above). Because this stage uses a single data source, no separate load or baseline restriction is needed here.

```{r}
#| label: s04b-mental-health-summary
mental_health_TP1 <- bind_rows(
  summarise_categorical(baseline_data, "SWEMWBS_Cat_TP1",           "Wellbeing (SWEMWBS band)"),
  summarise_categorical(baseline_data, "PHQ8_ProbableDepression_TP1", "Probable depression (PHQ-8)"),
  summarise_categorical(baseline_data, "GAD7_ProbableGAD_TP1",        "Probable anxiety (GAD-7)"),
  summarise_categorical(
    baseline_data |>
      mutate(ITQ_Category_TP1 = if_else(ITQ_Category_TP1 == "None", "Subclinical", ITQ_Category_TP1)),
    "ITQ_Category_TP1", "ITQ diagnostic category (ICD-11)"
  )
)

print(mental_health_TP1)
```

### Export

```{r}
#| label: s04b-export-tables
if (!dir.exists(here("data", "analysis"))) {
  dir.create(here("data", "analysis"), recursive = TRUE)
}

write_xlsx(
  list(
    Attrition                = attrition_table,
    Age_Continuous            = age_continuous,
    Demographics_Categorical  = demographics_categorical,
    Mental_Health_TP1         = mental_health_TP1
  ),
  here("data", "analysis", "participant_characteristics_TP1_TP4_TP5.xlsx")
)

message("Saved: data/analysis/participant_characteristics_TP1_TP4_TP5.xlsx")
```

# Stage 4c: Measure groups and labels (lookup)

## How this stage runs

**Reads:** nothing. This is a lookup and does not read any data.

**Writes:** `data/analysis/measure_groups.rdata`, loaded by stages 5, 6 and 8. Run this stage before stage 5, and run it again after any edit to the lookup table.

It records, once, how every Study 2 measure is grouped and labelled, so that stage 5 (tables), stage 6 (figure panels) and stage 8 (RCI bars) use the same groups, order, titles and axis labels.

1.  Defines one table, `measure_groups`, with one row per measure: domain, sub-group, correction family (Hypothesis 1 group), display order, the label spelling used in each script, chart title and y-axis label.
2.  Checks the table for mistakes (duplicate labels, missing domains).
3.  Defines `add_measure_groups()`, which attaches domain, sub-group, order and titles to any results table, and stops with the measure's name if a label is not in the lookup.
4.  Defines `measure_text()`, which returns one measure's chart title or y-axis label.
5.  Defines `measure_family()`, which returns a measure's correction family (`NA` for exploratory measures).
6.  Saves everything to `data/analysis/measure_groups.rdata`.

::: callout-note
**Display text only.** Nothing here changes a column name in the data. "BAT-12" appears in titles and axis labels only. Stages 1 to 4a are unaffected.
:::

The test chunks at the bottom of this stage check the lookup and its functions.

### Setup

```{r}
#| label: s04c-setup
#| message: false

library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(here)
```

### The lookup table

One row per measure. To add or rename a measure, this is the only place to edit.

| Column | Meaning |
|----|----|
| `key` | Stable internal name. Never shown in a figure or table |
| `label_three_tp` | Spelling in 05's `three_tp_measures$Label` and `descriptive_vars$Measure` |
| `label_two_tp` | Spelling in 05's `two_tp_lookup$Label` |
| `label_rci` | Spelling in 05's `rci_targets$Label` (`NA` where the measure is not in that table) |
| `domain` | Mental Health, Wellbeing, Occupational or Behavioural (from the project-context `measures.md`) |
| `sub_group` | Occupational only: Burnout, Work performance or Other occupational |
| `family` | Hypothesis 1 group used for correction: Mental health, Wellbeing, Behaviour or Workplace performance. `NA` for exploratory measures. Set below the table, not typed per row |
| `route` | `three_tp` (TP1, TP4, TP5) or `two_tp` (TP1, TP5) |
| `display_order` | Order within its domain (and sub-group) in tables and panels |
| `chart_title` | Panel title, thesis-ready |
| `y_label` | Y-axis label, thesis-ready |

```{r}
#| label: s04c-measure-groups-table
measure_groups <- tribble(
  ~key,            ~label_three_tp,             ~label_two_tp,                ~label_rci,                  ~domain,         ~sub_group,           ~route,      ~display_order, ~chart_title,                           ~y_label,
  # Mental Health
  "phq8",          "PHQ-8 Total",               NA,                           "PHQ-8",                     "Mental Health", NA,                   "three_tp",  1, "Depression Symptoms",                   "PHQ-8 Total Score",
  "gad7",          "GAD-7 Total",               NA,                           "GAD-7",                     "Mental Health", NA,                   "three_tp",  2, "Anxiety Symptoms",                      "GAD-7 Total Score",
  "itq_ptsd",      NA,                          "ITQ PTSD Total",             "ITQ PTSD",                  "Mental Health", NA,                   "two_tp",    3, "PTSD Symptoms",                         "ITQ PTSD Total Score",
  "itq_dso",       NA,                          "ITQ DSO Total",              "ITQ DSO",                   "Mental Health", NA,                   "two_tp",    4, "Disturbances in Self-Organisation",     "ITQ DSO Total Score",
  "itq_cptsd",     NA,                          "ITQ CPTSD Total",            "ITQ CPTSD",                 "Mental Health", NA,                   "two_tp",    5, "Complex PTSD Symptoms",                 "ITQ CPTSD Total Score",
  # Wellbeing
  "swemwbs",       "SWEMWBS Metric",            NA,                           "SWEMWBS",                   "Wellbeing",     NA,                   "three_tp",  1, "Psychological Wellbeing",               "SWEMWBS Metric Score",
  # Occupational: Burnout
  "bat_total",     "BAT Total Mean",            NA,                           "BAT Total",                 "Occupational",  "Burnout",            "three_tp",  1, "Burnout",                               "BAT-12 Total Mean Score",
  "bat_exh",       "BAT Exhaustion",            NA,                           "BAT Exhaustion",            "Occupational",  "Burnout",            "three_tp",  2, "Burnout: Exhaustion",                   "BAT-12 Exhaustion Score",
  "bat_mdist",     "BAT Mental Distance",       NA,                           "BAT Mental Distance",       "Occupational",  "Burnout",            "three_tp",  3, "Burnout: Mental Distance",              "BAT-12 Mental Distance Score",
  "bat_emo",       "BAT Emotional Impairment",  NA,                           "BAT Emotional Impairment",  "Occupational",  "Burnout",            "three_tp",  4, "Burnout: Emotional Impairment",         "BAT-12 Emotional Impairment Score",
  "bat_cog",       "BAT Cognitive Impairment",  NA,                           "BAT Cognitive Impairment",  "Occupational",  "Burnout",            "three_tp",  5, "Burnout: Cognitive Impairment",         "BAT-12 Cognitive Impairment Score",
  # Occupational: Work performance
  "hpq_abs",       NA,                          "HPQ Absenteeism Hours (4w)", NA,                          "Occupational",  "Work performance",   "two_tp",    1, "Absenteeism",                           "Absenteeism (hours, past 4 weeks)",
  "hpq_pres",      NA,                          "HPQ Presenteeism (%)",       "HPQ Presenteeism",          "Occupational",  "Work performance",   "two_tp",    2, "Presenteeism",                          "Presenteeism (%)",
  # Occupational: Other occupational
  "brs",           "BRS Mean",                  NA,                           "BRS",                       "Occupational",  "Other occupational", "three_tp",  1, "Resilience",                            "BRS Mean Score",
  "uwes",          "UWES Total",                NA,                           "UWES",                      "Occupational",  "Other occupational", "three_tp",  2, "Workplace Engagement",                  "UWES-3 Total Score",
  "oses",          "OSES Total",                NA,                           "OSES",                      "Occupational",  "Other occupational", "three_tp",  3, "Occupational Self-Efficacy",            "OSES Total Score",
  "intl",          "INTL Total",                NA,                           NA,                          "Occupational",  "Other occupational", "three_tp",  4, "Intention to Leave Work",               "Intention to Leave Total Score",
  # Behavioural
  "gspa",          "GSPA Total",                NA,                           "GSPA",                      "Behavioural",   NA,                   "three_tp",  1, "Physical Activity",                     "GSPA Total Score",
  "mhsis",         "MHSIS Mean",                NA,                           "MHSIS",                     "Behavioural",   NA,                   "three_tp",  2, "Help Seeking Intention",  "MHSIS Mean Score",
  "days_surfing",  NA,                          "Days Surfing per Month",     NA,                          "Behavioural",   NA,                   "two_tp",    3, "Days Surfing per Month",                "Days surfing per month"
) |>
  mutate(
    # Fixed factor levels make tables and figures sort in this order,
    # not alphabetically.
    domain    = factor(domain, levels = c("Mental Health", "Wellbeing", "Occupational", "Behavioural")),
    sub_group = factor(sub_group, levels = c("Burnout", "Work performance", "Other occupational"))
  )

# ---- Correction family (Hypothesis 1 group) ---------------------------------
# Each measure belongs to one Hypothesis 1 group, (a) to (d). Bonferroni
# correction is applied within each group in stage 5. Measures listed in
# exploratory_keys are in no hypothesis, so their family is NA and they are
# never corrected. To change which measures are exploratory, edit that vector.

exploratory_keys <- c("days_surfing", "intl")

family_names <- c(
  "Mental Health" = "Mental health",
  "Wellbeing"     = "Wellbeing",
  "Behavioural"   = "Behaviour",
  "Occupational"  = "Workplace performance"
)

# Order the four families appear in, in tables.
family_order <- unname(family_names[c("Mental Health", "Wellbeing", "Behavioural", "Occupational")])

measure_groups <- measure_groups |>
  mutate(
    family = if_else(
      key %in% exploratory_keys,
      NA_character_,
      unname(family_names[as.character(domain)])
    )
  )
```

### Alias table

Turns the three label columns into one long list of "label to key" pairs, so a label from any script can be matched to its measure.

Some measures use the same spelling in more than one script (the four BAT sub-scales are spelled identically in the three-timepoint list and the RCI list). That is fine, because both spellings point to the same measure. `distinct()` collapses those repeats into one row. The check in the next section then only complains if one label points to two different measures.

```{r}
#| label: s04c-measure-aliases
measure_aliases <- measure_groups |>
  select(key, label_three_tp, label_two_tp, label_rci) |>
  pivot_longer(-key, names_to = "spelling", values_to = "alias", values_drop_na = TRUE) |>
  distinct(key, alias)
```

### Checks on the lookup itself

If the table above is edited badly, this chunk stops the render with a message naming the problem.

```{r}
#| label: s04c-check-lookup
dup_keys <- measure_groups$key[duplicated(measure_groups$key)]
if (length(dup_keys) > 0) {
  stop("measure_groups: duplicated key(s): ", paste(dup_keys, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
}

dup_alias <- measure_aliases |>
  count(alias) |>
  filter(n > 1) |>
  pull(alias)
if (length(dup_alias) > 0) {
  stop("measure_groups: the same label points to more than one measure: ",
       paste(dup_alias, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
}

missing_domain <- measure_groups$key[is.na(measure_groups$domain)]
if (length(missing_domain) > 0) {
  stop("measure_groups: no domain (or a misspelt domain) for: ",
       paste(missing_domain, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
}

occ_no_sub <- measure_groups |>
  filter(domain == "Occupational", is.na(sub_group)) |>
  pull(key)
if (length(occ_no_sub) > 0) {
  stop("measure_groups: Occupational measure(s) with no sub_group: ",
       paste(occ_no_sub, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
}

cat("✅ Lookup checks passed:", nrow(measure_groups), "measures,",
    nrow(measure_aliases), "label spellings.\n")
```

### Function: attach groups to any results table

`add_measure_groups(data, "Label")` takes any table with a column of measure labels (give the column's name as text) and adds domain, sub-group, route, display order, chart title and y-axis label. Rows come back sorted by domain, sub-group and display order.

It stops, naming the label, if any label in `data` is not in the lookup. This is deliberate: a silent mismatch cannot pass through to the figures. A measure with no figure or group (for example Surf Before/After) must be removed from the table before calling it.

```{r}
#| label: s04c-fn-add-measure-groups
add_measure_groups <- function(data, label_col = "Label") {
  labels_in_data <- unique(data[[label_col]])
  unknown <- setdiff(labels_in_data, measure_aliases$alias)

  if (length(unknown) > 0) {
    stop("No domain found in the stage 4c lookup for: ",
         paste0("'", unknown, "'", collapse = ", "),
         ". Check the spelling, or add the measure to measure_groups.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  data |>
    left_join(
      measure_aliases |> select(key, alias),
      by = set_names("alias", label_col),
      relationship = "many-to-one"
    ) |>
    left_join(
      measure_groups |> select(key, domain, sub_group, family, route, display_order,
                               chart_title, y_label),
      by = "key",
      relationship = "many-to-one"
    ) |>
    arrange(domain, sub_group, display_order)
}
```

### Function: one measure's title or y-axis label

`measure_text(label, "chart_title")` or `measure_text(label, "y_label")` returns the text for one measure, whichever spelling of its label you pass. It stops if the label is unknown, so a raw label is never shown by accident.

```{r}
#| label: s04c-fn-measure-text
measure_text <- function(label, what = c("chart_title", "y_label")) {
  what <- match.arg(what)
  key <- measure_aliases$key[match(label, measure_aliases$alias)]
  if (is.na(key)) {
    stop("No entry in the stage 4c lookup for: '", label, "'", call. = FALSE)
  }
  measure_groups[[what]][measure_groups$key == key]
}
```

### Function: correction family for a list of measures

`measure_family(labels)` takes a column of measure labels (any spelling) and returns each measure's correction family: "Mental health", "Wellbeing", "Behaviour" or "Workplace performance". It returns `NA` for the exploratory measures (Days Surfing per Month, Intention to Leave), which are never corrected. It stops, naming the label, if a label is not in the lookup.

```{r}
#| label: s04c-fn-measure-family
measure_family <- function(labels) {
  unknown <- setdiff(unique(labels), measure_aliases$alias)
  if (length(unknown) > 0) {
    stop("No entry in the stage 4c lookup for: ",
         paste0("'", unknown, "'", collapse = ", "),
         call. = FALSE)
  }
  keys <- measure_aliases$key[match(labels, measure_aliases$alias)]
  measure_groups$family[match(keys, measure_groups$key)]
}
```

### Save for 05 and 06

Stages 5, 6 and 8 load this with `load(here("data", "analysis", "measure_groups.rdata"))`. This stage must be run first, and again after any edit to the table.

```{r}
#| label: s04c-save-measure-groups
if (!dir.exists(here("data", "analysis"))) {
  dir.create(here("data", "analysis"), recursive = TRUE)
}

save(
  measure_groups,
  measure_aliases,
  add_measure_groups,
  measure_text,
  measure_family,
  family_order,
  file = here("data", "analysis", "measure_groups.rdata")
)

message("Saved: data/analysis/measure_groups.rdata")
```

### Tests

Run these once after rendering. Each has an expected result stated above it.

#### Test 1: table order

Expect 20 rows, in Mental Health, Wellbeing, Occupational, Behavioural order, with Occupational split into Burnout, Work performance, Other occupational.

```{r}
#| label: s04c-test-order
measure_groups |>
  arrange(domain, sub_group, display_order) |>
  select(domain, sub_group, key, chart_title) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

#### Test 2: titles and axis labels

Expect "Burnout", then "BAT-12 Total Mean Score", then "Depression Symptoms" twice (one measure, two spellings).

```{r}
#| label: s04c-test-text
measure_text("BAT Total Mean", "chart_title")
measure_text("BAT Total Mean", "y_label")
measure_text("PHQ-8 Total", "chart_title")
measure_text("PHQ-8", "chart_title")
```

#### Test 3: an unknown label must stop

Expect an error naming 'Surf Before After'. `try()` lets the document keep rendering after showing the message.

```{r}
#| label: s04c-test-unknown
try(add_measure_groups(tibble(Label = c("PHQ-8 Total", "Surf Before After"))))
```

#### Test 4: a known label must work

Expect two rows, both Mental Health.

```{r}
#| label: s04c-test-known
add_measure_groups(tibble(Label = c("PHQ-8 Total", "ITQ PTSD Total"))) |>
  select(Label, domain, chart_title)
```

#### Test 5: correction families

Expect five rows: Mental health 5 measures, Wellbeing 1, Behaviour 2, Workplace performance 10, and `NA` 2 (Days Surfing and Intention to Leave, the exploratory measures). Then two checks: the first should return "Workplace performance", the second `NA`.

```{r}
#| label: s04c-test-family
measure_groups |>
  count(family)

measure_family("BAT Total Mean")
measure_family("Days Surfing per Month")
```

#### Test 6: your real 05 tables

This is the important test. It cannot run in this stage, because the three tables live in 05. Once they exist in 05, run these three lines there after loading `measure_groups.rdata`. Each should return without an error. If one stops, its message names the label that does not match, and that spelling needs fixing in the lookup table above.

``` r
add_measure_groups(three_tp_measures, "Label")
add_measure_groups(two_tp_lookup, "Label")
add_measure_groups(rci_targets, "Label")
```

# Stage 5: Statistical analysis

## How this stage runs

**Reads:** `data/clean/scored_data.rds` and `data/analysis/measure_groups.rdata` (stage 4c).

**Writes:** `data/analysis/analysis_results.rdata` (the handoff for stages 6 and 8), `data/analysis/test_results_summary.xlsx`, and a normality-override template in `data/analysis/`.

**This stage is interactive.** It contains outlier checks and a test-recommendation check that pause for a y/n answer, and a normality-override step that needs you to edit an Excel file between two chunks. Run it chunk by chunk from the console. It stops with an error if rendered unattended.

What it does:

1.  **Descriptive statistics:** mean, SD and n for every outcome at every timepoint it was collected at.
2.  **Two-timepoint measures (TP1 vs TP5 only):** ITQ (PTSD, DSO and CPTSD totals), HPQ (absenteeism hours, presenteeism percent) and Days Surfing per Month. An outlier check on the TP5 minus TP1 difference (1.5×IQR rule), a Shapiro-Wilk normality test on that difference, then a paired t-test (if normal) or a Wilcoxon signed-rank test (if not). The effect size reported is whichever the test naturally produces.
3.  **Three-timepoint measures (TP1, TP4, TP5):** SWEMWBS, PHQ-8, GAD-7, MHSIS, BRS, UWES, OSES, BAT Total plus 4 subscales, GSPA and Intention to Leave. An outlier check on raw scores per timepoint with `rstatix::identify_outliers()`, Shapiro-Wilk normality per timepoint, then a repeated-measures ANOVA with Greenhouse-Geisser correction (generalised eta-squared as the effect size) if normal, or a Friedman test (Kendall's *W*) if not. Pairwise post-hoc comparisons follow, but only for measures whose omnibus test was significant.
4.  **Multiple-testing correction:** Bonferroni within each hypothesis group (Mental health, Wellbeing, Behaviour, Workplace performance). Days Surfing per Month and Intention to Leave are exploratory and are not corrected.
5.  **Surf Before/After:** descriptive only (percentage answering "yes" at each timepoint). This variable is binary, and no inferential test is run on it.
6.  **RCI (Reliable Change Index):** Jacobson-Truax classification for 17 targets through one classifier: SWEMWBS, PHQ-8, GAD-7, MHSIS, BRS, UWES, OSES, BAT Total plus 4 subscales, GSPA, ITQ PTSD Total, ITQ DSO Total, ITQ CPTSD Total and HPQ Presenteeism, all run as ordinary continuous measures with no diagnostic-category logic. TP1 vs TP4 and TP1 vs TP5 are compared where both exist. ITQ and HPQ Presenteeism are TP1 vs TP5 only, because neither is administered at TP4. Reliability for 15 targets is Cronbach's alpha computed from TP1 item data, with item groupings matching each RCI target. GSPA and HPQ Presenteeism use sourced values (0.74 and 0.89), because neither is a multi-item scale in the Cronbach's sense. INTL and HPQ Absenteeism are **not** in the RCI. INTL is a 2-item, self-made, unvalidated measure that does not support a trustworthy reliability estimate, and HPQ Absenteeism has no defensible single reliability value in the published literature for a population close to this one. Both get scatter plots in stage 6. This stage does the calculation and classification only. The RCI plots are in stage 6 and stage 8.
7.  **Export:** everything goes to one combined `.xlsx` workbook with separate sheets, and an `.rdata` handoff is saved so stages 6 and 8 can plot without re-running any of this.

### Setup

```{r}

#| message: false

library(clinicalsignificance)
```

### Load scored data

```{r}

```

### Timepoint labels

Used consistently in every table and every plot caption in this pipeline.

```{r}
#| label: s05-timepoint-labels
tp_labels <- c(TP1 = "1-Week Before", TP4 = "2-Week Follow-Up", TP5 = "3-Month Follow-Up")
```

### Measure groups and table sorting

Results tables below are sorted by measure domain (Mental Health, Wellbeing, Occupational, Behavioural), then by sub-group and display order, using the lookup built in stage 4c. That stage must be run first. Sorting happens after each table is computed, so no statistic, Bonferroni family or test decision depends on the order.

`sort_by_domain()` keeps every original column and only re-orders the rows. It stops, naming the label, if a measure is not in the lookup. Setting `show_groups = TRUE` adds `Domain` and `Sub_group` columns beside the measure name; the default leaves the columns exactly as they were.

```{r}
#| label: s05-measure-groups-sort
load(here("data", "analysis", "measure_groups.rdata"))

# measure_family() and family_order come from the measure lookup (stage 4c).
# An older saved file will not have them.
if (!exists("measure_family") || !exists("family_order")) {
  stop("measure_groups.rdata is out of date. Re-run stage 4c first.")
}

sort_by_domain <- function(data, label_col = "Measure", show_groups = FALSE) {
  # Nothing to sort (for example, no significant omnibus test, so the post-hoc
  # tables are empty): return as is.
  if (nrow(data) == 0) return(data)

  original_cols <- names(data)
  sorted <- add_measure_groups(data, label_col)

  if (show_groups) {
    sorted |>
      mutate(Domain = domain, Sub_group = sub_group) |>
      select(all_of(label_col), Domain, Sub_group,
             all_of(setdiff(original_cols, label_col)))
  } else {
    sorted |> select(all_of(original_cols))
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: s05-compute-descriptives
descriptives_table <- descriptive_vars |>
  mutate(
    Mean = map_dbl(Column, ~ mean(scored_data[[.x]], na.rm = TRUE)),
    SD   = map_dbl(Column, ~ sd(scored_data[[.x]], na.rm = TRUE)),
    N    = map_dbl(Column, ~ sum(!is.na(scored_data[[.x]])))

  mutate(
    Timepoint_Label = tp_labels[Timepoint],
    Mean = round(Mean, 2),
    SD   = round(SD, 2)
  ) |>
  select(Measure, Timepoint, Timepoint_Label, Mean, SD, N) |>
  sort_by_domain("Measure")

print(descriptives_table)
```

## Part 2 — Two-timepoint measures (TP1 vs TP5)

ITQ (PTSD/DSO/CPTSD), HPQ (absenteeism hours, presenteeism percent), and Days Surfing per Month. These only have TP1 and TP5 data, so they follow a paired-difference route, and not the three-timepoint RM-ANOVA route below.

### Compute difference scores

```{r}
#| label: s05-two-tp-compute-differences
two_tp_data <- scored_data |>
  mutate(
    Diff_ITQ_PTSD_Total            = ITQ_PTSD_Total_TP5 - ITQ_PTSD_Total_TP1,
    Diff_ITQ_DSO_Total             = ITQ_DSO_Total_TP5 - ITQ_DSO_Total_TP1,
    Diff_ITQ_CPTSD_Total           = ITQ_CPTSD_Total_TP5 - ITQ_CPTSD_Total_TP1,
    Diff_HPQ_Absenteeism_Hours     = HPQ_absenteeism_hours_4w_TP5 - HPQ_absenteeism_hours_4w_TP1,
    Diff_HPQ_Presenteeism_Percent  = HPQ_presenteeism_percent_TP5 - HPQ_presenteeism_percent_TP1,
    Diff_DaysSurfingMonth          = DaysSurfingMonth_TP5 - DaysSurfingMonth_TP1
  )

# Lookup so the test loop below knows which TP1/TP5 columns and display label
# go with each Diff_ column.
two_tp_lookup <- tribble(
  ~DiffCol,                         ~PreCol,                          ~PostCol,                          ~Label,                         ~Direction,
  "Diff_ITQ_PTSD_Total",            "ITQ_PTSD_Total_TP1",             "ITQ_PTSD_Total_TP5",             "ITQ PTSD Total",              "Lower = Improvement",
  "Diff_ITQ_DSO_Total",             "ITQ_DSO_Total_TP1",              "ITQ_DSO_Total_TP5",              "ITQ DSO Total",               "Lower = Improvement",
  "Diff_ITQ_CPTSD_Total",           "ITQ_CPTSD_Total_TP1",            "ITQ_CPTSD_Total_TP5",            "ITQ CPTSD Total",             "Lower = Improvement",
  "Diff_HPQ_Absenteeism_Hours",     "HPQ_absenteeism_hours_4w_TP1",   "HPQ_absenteeism_hours_4w_TP5",   "HPQ Absenteeism Hours (4w)",  "Lower = Improvement",
  "Diff_HPQ_Presenteeism_Percent",  "HPQ_presenteeism_percent_TP1",   "HPQ_presenteeism_percent_TP5",   "HPQ Presenteeism (%)",        "Higher = Improvement",
  "Diff_DaysSurfingMonth",          "DaysSurfingMonth_TP1",           "DaysSurfingMonth_TP5",           "Days Surfing per Month",      "Higher = Improvement"
)
```

### Visual outlier check

::: callout-note
**Scatter, histogram, and boxplot code style adapted from Field, A., & Field, A. (2026). *Discovering statistics using R & RStudio* (2nd ed.). Sage. (pp. 364–365).** Colour and theme conventions adapted to match this pipeline's established `theme_classic()`/greyscale style, rather than reproduced exactly as printed in the source.
:::

One scatter, one histogram, and one boxplot per two-timepoint measure, run before the numeric 1.5×IQR check below so you have a chance to look at the shape of the data — and spot-check any specific point — before answering that check's y/n prompt. The boxplot whiskers are drawn at exactly 1.5×IQR beyond the box — the same rule the numeric check below applies, shown visually here first rather than only reported afterwards as a table of flagged IDs.

```{r}
#| label: s05-two-tp-outlier-visual-check
#| results: asis

for (i in seq_len(nrow(two_tp_lookup))) {

  pre_col  <- two_tp_lookup$PreCol[i]
  post_col <- two_tp_lookup$PostCol[i]
  diff_col <- two_tp_lookup$DiffCol[i]
  label    <- two_tp_lookup$Label[i]

  # Scatter: TP1 vs TP5, with a dotted "no change" diagonal reference line.
  # Points far from the diagonal represent a large pre-post change — the
  # same thing the 1.5xIQR rule below flags numerically, made visible here.
  plot_scatter <- ggplot(two_tp_data, aes(x = .data[[pre_col]], y = .data[[post_col]])) +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
    geom_point(fill = "grey70", colour = "black", shape = 21, alpha = 0.7) +
    labs(
      title = paste(label, "— 1-Week Before vs 3-Month Follow-Up"),
      x     = "1-Week Before (TP1) score",
      y     = "3-Month Follow-Up (TP5) score"
    ) +
    theme_classic()

  # Histogram: shape of the difference score distribution — the same
  # variable the numeric outlier check below operates on.
  plot_hist <- ggplot(two_tp_data, aes(x = .data[[diff_col]])) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 15, fill = "grey70", colour = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
    labs(
      title = paste(label, "— Difference Score (TP5 − TP1)"),
      x     = "Difference (TP5 − TP1)",
      y     = "Count"
    ) +
    theme_classic()

  # Boxplot: whiskers = 1.5xIQR beyond the box, by ggplot2's default —
  # this is the outlier rule from the block below, drawn rather than tabulated.
  plot_box <- ggplot(two_tp_data, aes(x = "", y = .data[[diff_col]])) +
    geom_boxplot(fill = "grey70", colour = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
    labs(
      title = paste(label, "— Difference Score Boxplot"),
      x     = NULL,
      y     = "Difference (TP5 − TP1)"
    ) +
    theme_classic()

  print(plot_scatter)
  print(plot_hist)
  print(plot_box)
}
```

### Outlier detection

The 1.5×IQR rule is applied to each difference score, with a `stop()` and an interactive y/n prompt if any outliers are found. The y/n prompt only works if you run this chunk yourself in the console (see the run notes at the top of this document). The scatter, histogram and boxplot set above runs first, so you can look at the shape of the data and identify specific points before the prompt appears.

::: callout-note
**Outlier check on the difference score.** This uses `rstatix::identify_outliers()`, as in Part 3, applied to the TP5 minus TP1 difference, because that is the variable the paired t-test or Wilcoxon test actually analyses. It separates regular outliers (beyond 1.5×IQR) from extreme outliers (beyond 3×IQR).
:::

```{r}
#| label: s05-two-tp-outlier-detection
two_tp_outliers <- map(seq_len(nrow(two_tp_lookup)), function(i) {
  two_tp_data |>
    select(ID, all_of(two_tp_lookup$DiffCol[i])) |>
    identify_outliers(all_of(two_tp_lookup$DiffCol[i]))
})
names(two_tp_outliers) <- two_tp_lookup$Label

any_outliers <- any(map_lgl(two_tp_outliers, ~ nrow(.x) > 0))

if (any_outliers) {

  print("❌ Outliers detected in the following variables:")
  for (label in names(two_tp_outliers)) {
    if (nrow(two_tp_outliers[[label]]) > 0) {
      cat("\n---", label, "---\n")
      print(two_tp_outliers[[label]])
    }
  }

  if (interactive()) {
    response <- readline(prompt = "Outliers detected (see above). Continue anyway? (y/n): ")
    if (!tolower(trimws(response)) %in% c("y", "yes")) {
      stop("Analysis stopped after reviewing outliers. Re-run this chunk and answer 'y' to continue, or address the outliers first.")
    }
    print("Continuing with analysis — outliers were reviewed and accepted.")
  } else {
    stop("Outliers detected — see the table above. Rendering stops here because there is no way to confirm continuation during a non-interactive render. Run this chunk interactively in the console first to review and confirm before rendering the full document.")
  }

} else {
  print("✅ No outliers detected in any difference variable. Data is ready for analysis!")
}
```

### Normality tests

Shapiro-Wilk gives you a formal p-value, but it's easy for it to disagree with what a difference score's distribution actually looks like — a large sample can return a "significant" (non-normal) result for a distribution that's only mildly skewed, and a small sample can return "normal" for something that clearly isn't. Skewness, kurtosis, and the histograms below are for judging that by eye alongside the p-value, not for a formal decision rule.

::: callout-note
**Skewness and kurtosis** come from `psych::skew()` and `psych::kurtosi()` with `type = 2` stated explicitly. The three standard estimators (types 1, 2 and 3) give different numbers for the same data (Joanes, D. N., & Gill, C. A. (1998). Comparing measures of sample skewness and kurtosis. *Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series D*, 47(1), 183–189). Type 2 is the bias-adjusted estimator used by SPSS and SAS. `kurtosi()` returns excess kurtosis, so 0 means normal-tailed.
:::

```{r}
#| label: s05-two-tp-normality-tests
two_tp_shapiro <- two_tp_data |>
  select(all_of(two_tp_lookup$DiffCol)) |>
  map(shapiro.test)

two_tp_shapiro_df <- data.frame(
  DiffCol     = names(two_tp_shapiro),
  W_Statistic = sapply(two_tp_shapiro, function(x) x$statistic),
  P_Value     = sapply(two_tp_shapiro, function(x) x$p.value)
) |>
  mutate(
    Skewness         = sapply(DiffCol, function(v) round(psych::skew(two_tp_data[[v]], type = 2, na.rm = TRUE), 2)),
    Excess_Kurtosis  = sapply(DiffCol, function(v) round(psych::kurtosi(two_tp_data[[v]], type = 2, na.rm = TRUE), 2))
  )

print(two_tp_shapiro_df)
```

### Normality histograms

One histogram per difference score, with the Shapiro-Wilk p-value, skewness, and excess kurtosis all shown together so you can check them against the shape by eye.

```{r}
#| label: s05-two-tp-normality-histograms
#| results: asis

for (diff_var in two_tp_shapiro_df$DiffCol) {

  p_val <- two_tp_shapiro_df$P_Value[two_tp_shapiro_df$DiffCol == diff_var]
  skew  <- two_tp_shapiro_df$Skewness[two_tp_shapiro_df$DiffCol == diff_var]
  kurt  <- two_tp_shapiro_df$Excess_Kurtosis[two_tp_shapiro_df$DiffCol == diff_var]

  p <- ggplot(two_tp_data, aes(x = .data[[diff_var]])) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 15, fill = "steelblue", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
    labs(
      title    = paste("Histogram of", diff_var),
      subtitle = paste0("Shapiro-Wilk p: ", signif(p_val, 3),
                         "  |  Skewness: ", skew,
                         "  |  Excess kurtosis: ", kurt),
      x        = diff_var,
      y        = "Count"
    ) +
    theme_classic()

  print(p)
}
```

### Q-Q plots

::: callout-note
**Q-Q plot code is adapted from Field, A., & Field, A. (2026). *Discovering statistics using R & RStudio* (2nd ed.). Sage. (p. 380).** The source uses `qqplotr` to add a confidence band around the reference line. This script uses base `ggplot2`'s `stat_qq()` and `stat_qq_line()` instead, which draw the same line and points without the band. Colours and theme follow the `theme_classic()` greyscale convention used throughout.
:::

One Q-Q plot per difference score. Points falling close to the diagonal line support normality; points curving away from it, especially at the extremes, is what skew or heavy/light tails look like on this type of plot — the same signal the skewness/kurtosis figures above are quantifying, shown visually instead.

```{r}
#| label: s05-two-tp-qq-plots
#| results: asis

for (diff_var in two_tp_shapiro_df$DiffCol) {

  p <- ggplot(two_tp_data, aes(sample = .data[[diff_var]])) +
    stat_qq(color = "grey40", alpha = 0.7, size = 1.5) +
    stat_qq_line(color = "black", linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(
      title = paste("Q-Q Plot —", diff_var),
      x     = "Theoretical quantiles",
      y     = "Sample quantiles"
    ) +
    theme_classic()

  print(p)
}
```

### Test recommendation and human-in-the-loop check

**Decision rule for the recommended test:** if Shapiro-Wilk is non-significant (p \> .05), treat the difference as normal and recommend a paired t-test. If Shapiro-Wilk **is** significant (p ≤ .05), check skewness and kurtosis before accepting that verdict — if skewness falls within ±1 and excess kurtosis falls within ±2, treat this as Shapiro-Wilk being oversensitive for this sample size and recommend a paired t-test anyway. Only if skewness or kurtosis falls outside those ranges too does it fall through to a Wilcoxon signed-rank recommendation. Every row records which path it took (`Decision_Basis`) so this is checkable afterwards, not hidden inside the branching logic.

::: callout-note
**Skewness and kurtosis override.** If Shapiro-Wilk is significant but skewness is within ±1 and excess kurtosis is within ±2, the difference is treated as close enough to normal for a paired t-test. The rationale is that Shapiro-Wilk becomes sensitive to small departures from normality as sample size grows, so it can flag mild skew even when a t-test is robust. The thresholds are a researcher's decision. Some measures may therefore be t-tested despite a significant Shapiro-Wilk result. The histograms, skewness and kurtosis figures and Q-Q plots above are what justify that choice, so cite them, and not only the Shapiro-Wilk p-value, when reporting test selection.
:::

::: callout-note
**Human-in-the-loop check.** This chunk only recommends a test per measure and then stops for confirmation. It gives a deliberate pause to review the Q-Q plots and histograms above before the test runs, especially for any row whose `Decision_Basis` mentions an override. It uses the same interactive y/n convention as the outlier checks, so run it yourself in the console. It cannot run in an unattended render.
:::

```{r}
#| label: s05-two-tp-test-recommendation
two_tp_test_recommendations <- data.frame(
  Measure          = character(),
  Use_TTest        = logical(),
  Recommended_Test = character(),
  Decision_Basis   = character(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(two_tp_lookup))) {

  diff_col <- two_tp_lookup$DiffCol[i]
  label    <- two_tp_lookup$Label[i]

  shapiro_p <- two_tp_shapiro_df$P_Value[two_tp_shapiro_df$DiffCol == diff_col]
```
