# Stage 6: Figures

## How this stage runs

**Reads:** `data/analysis/analysis_results.rdata` (stage 5) and `data/analysis/measure_groups.rdata` (stage 4c).

**Writes:** all figures, to `data/analysis/`.

No statistics are recalculated here. Results are loaded and plotted.

Figures:

- **Bar-chart figures, one per hypothesis group** (mean ± 95% CI at each timepoint, one panel per measure). The groups are the four in Hypothesis 1 of the project-context skill, taken from the `family` and `domain` columns in stage 4c:
  - **Mental Health:** PHQ-8 and GAD-7 (three timepoints) above ITQ PTSD, DSO and CPTSD (two timepoints), in one figure.
  - **Wellbeing:** SWEMWBS, one panel.
  - **Behaviour:** GSPA and MHSIS.
  - **Workplace Performance,** split into three figures: Burnout (BAT-12 total and four subscales); Absenteeism and Presenteeism; Resilience, Engagement, Self-Efficacy and Intention to Leave.
- **Exploratory bar chart:** Days Surfing per Month, on its own. It and Intention to Leave are in no hypothesis group and are not corrected for multiple testing. Each panel's caption line says so.
- **RCI scatter plots**, using the classifications stage 5 computed (`rci_results`). ITQ PTSD, DSO and CPTSD and HPQ Presenteeism are TP1 vs TP5 only. Colours are not greyscale here, which is the one exception to the greyscale rule used elsewhere.
- **INTL scatter** and **HPQ Absenteeism scatter.** These measures are not in the RCI (see stage 5).

There is no Surf Before/After figure, because that variable is descriptive only.

### Setup

```{r}
#| label: s06-setup
#| message: false

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(here)

load(here("data", "analysis", "analysis_results.rdata"))
load(here("data", "analysis", "measure_groups.rdata"))

# measure_family() (stage 4c) and correction_family_summary (stage 5) are needed
# here. Older saved files will not have them.
if (!exists("measure_family") || !exists("correction_family_summary")) {
  stop("Re-run stages 4c and 5 first.")
}
```

### Chart labelling and measure groups

Every panel title and y-axis label comes from the lookup saved by stage 4c, through `measure_text()`. Nothing is hand-typed here. Panel titles show the construct (for example "Depression Symptoms"), and the y-axis names the instrument and scale (for example "PHQ-8 Total Score", "BAT-12 Total Mean Score"). The lookup holds every spelling of each measure's label (bar-chart spelling and RCI spelling), so one call serves both. If a label is not in the lookup, `measure_text()` stops and names it, so a raw label is never shown by accident.

Which measures sit in which figure also comes from the lookup (`labels_in()` below), using each measure's domain, sub-group and route.

```{r}
#| label: s06-construct-labels
construct_title   <- function(label) measure_text(label, "chart_title")
construct_y_label <- function(label) measure_text(label, "y_label")

# Labels of the measures in one figure group, in display order. `dom` is a
# domain from 04c (Mental Health, Wellbeing, Occupational, Behavioural);
# `route_type` is "three_tp" or "two_tp", which decides which spelling of the
# label is returned (the spelling stage 5 uses for that route); `sub` is an
# Occupational sub-group (Burnout, Work performance, Other occupational).
labels_in <- function(dom, route_type, sub = NULL) {
  group <- measure_groups |> filter(domain == dom, route == route_type)
  if (!is.null(sub)) group <- group |> filter(sub_group == sub)
  group <- group |> arrange(display_order)
  if (route_type == "three_tp") group$label_three_tp else group$label_two_tp
}

# One sentence for a figure caption saying which correction family its
# measures were corrected in and how big that family turned out to be.
correction_note <- function(family) {
  row <- correction_family_summary |> filter(Family == family)
  if (nrow(row) == 0 || row$N_Tests == 0) return("")
  paste0("Bonferroni correction is applied within the ", tolower(family), " hypothesis group (",
         row$N_Tests, " tests, threshold p < ", sprintf("%.4f", row$Bonferroni_Threshold), ").")
}

note_posthoc <- paste(
  "Brackets show Bonferroni-corrected post-hoc comparisons, shown only where the omnibus test was significant.",
  "For these measures the p-value listed is the omnibus test."
)
note_two_tp <- "For measures at two timepoints, the p-value listed is the Bonferroni-corrected paired test."
```

## Part 1 — Two-timepoint panel function and figure legend helpers

Each two-timepoint panel shows the mean at 1-Week Before and 3-Month Follow-Up with 95% CI error bars (±1.96 × SEM) and a significance marker from `two_tp_test_summary`. Each panel's own title and y-axis are the only text on the panel itself. The p-value, paired N and the measure's `Direction` (as "desired direction = increase/decrease") sit in the figure caption, one line per panel. The direction wording describes which way the bars need to move and says nothing about what was found. Figures themselves are built further down, in Part 2, by hypothesis group.

### Reusable panel-building function

::: callout-note
**One function per panel type.** Each panel type (two-timepoint and three-timepoint) is written once as a function and called once per measure, so a fix or style change is made in one place.
:::

```{r}
#| label: s06-desired-change-helper
# Shared by both build_two_tp_panel() and build_three_tp_panel(). Translates
# this measure's static Direction string (e.g. "Lower = Improvement" /
# "Higher = Improvement") into a plain "increase"/"decrease" word, which feeds
# the group figure's caption (see format_legend_line() below). It describes
# which way the bars need to move for a desired change. It is not a claim about
# what actually happened or whether it was significant (that is reported in the
# text, not on the chart). It is its own function so both panel builders use
# the identical rule.
parse_desired_change <- function(direction, label) {
  if (grepl("^Lower", direction, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    "decrease"
  } else if (grepl("^Higher", direction, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    "increase"
  } else {
    stop(
      "parse_desired_change(): unrecognised Direction value '", direction,
      "' for measure '", label, "' — expected it to start with ",
      "'Lower' or 'Higher'. Check the lookup table."
    )
  }
}
```

### Figure legend helpers

::: callout-note
**Figure captions carry the test information.** Panel titles are unbold and centred. The p-value, n and desired direction for each panel are printed in the group figure's caption, one line per panel. This is a working note for the researcher to read off while writing the figure legend, so the wording is plain and literal (`"<Construct>: p = <value>, n = <n>, desired direction = <increase/decrease>."`) and does not follow APA figure-legend conventions.
:::

```{r}
#| label: s06-legend-caption-helpers
# One line of the caption per panel: construct title (same lookup the
# panel's own title uses, so the caption and the panel titles read
# consistently), p-value, n, and desired direction of change. A
# measure in no hypothesis group (Days Surfing per Month, Intention to Leave)
# gets an extra sentence saying it is exploratory and not corrected.
format_legend_line <- function(label, p_value, n, direction) {
  chart_title <- construct_title(label)
  desired_change <- parse_desired_change(direction, label)
  line <- paste0(chart_title, ": p = ", p_value, ", n = ", n, ", desired direction = ", desired_change, ".")
  if (is.na(measure_family(label))) {
    line <- paste(line, "Exploratory measure, not corrected for multiple testing.")
  }
  line
}

# Joins a group's per-panel lines with the fixed error-bar/significance
# explanation. `extra` (a single string or several) adds further trailing
# notes. The whole caption is wrapped to `width` characters per line,
# so a long caption is not cut off at the figure's edge.
build_group_legend <- function(lines, extra = NULL, width = 110) {
  text <- paste(
    paste(lines, collapse = " "),
    "Error bars = 95% CI (±1.96 × SEM). (* p < .05).",
    paste(extra, collapse = " ")
  )
  paste(strwrap(text, width = width), collapse = "\n")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: s06-two-tp-panel-function
# Builds one bar-chart panel for a single two-timepoint measure.
# Takes the pre/post column names, the display label, the direction text,
# the raw data (two_tp_data) to compute the mean/SD/N from, and the test
# results table (two_tp_test_summary) to pull the significance marker from.
# y_breaks_width is optional (default NULL = ggplot's automatic breaks);
# pass a number to force gridlines at that fixed interval, e.g. so two
# panels with different y-axis maxima still share the same increment
# (used for the ITQ PTSD/DSO panels, see below).
build_two_tp_panel <- function(pre_col, post_col, label, direction, data, test_summary, y_breaks_width = NULL) {

  # Step 1: reshape just these two columns into long format, one row per
  # person per timepoint, then compute mean, SD, N and SEM at each timepoint.
  summary_stats <- data |>
    select(all_of(c(pre_col, post_col))) |>
    pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "col", values_to = "value") |>
    mutate(Timepoint = if_else(col == pre_col, "TP1", "TP5")) |>
    filter(!is.na(value)) |>
    summarise(
      Mean = mean(value),
      SD   = sd(value),
      N    = n(),
      SEM  = SD / sqrt(N),
      .by  = Timepoint
    ) |>
    mutate(Timepoint = factor(Timepoint, levels = c("TP1", "TP5"),
                               labels = unname(tp_labels[c("TP1", "TP5")])))

  # Step 2: pull this measure's own row from the already-computed test
  # results, so the p-value and test name shown on the chart match the
  # official numbers in the exported .xlsx exactly.
  test_row <- test_summary |> filter(Measure == label)

  # Uses P_Value_Bonferroni, the corrected p-value. That is corrected within this
  # measure's hypothesis group (see 05's Part 3 callout). For an exploratory
  # measure (Days Surfing per Month) it is simply the raw p-value, because 05 does
  # not correct those.
  #
  # "<0.001" doesn't convert to a number, so it's checked for separately;
  # suppressWarnings() just silences the harmless coercion warning that
  # would otherwise print every time this runs on a "<0.001" row.
  is_sig <- if (test_row$P_Value_Bonferroni == "<0.001") {
    TRUE
  } else {
    suppressWarnings(as.numeric(test_row$P_Value_Bonferroni)) < 0.05
  }
  sig_label <- if (isTRUE(is_sig)) "*" else "ns"

  y_max <- max(summary_stats$Mean + 1.96 * summary_stats$SEM)

  # This measure's construct title and y-axis label, from the 04c lookup.
  # Stops, naming the label, if it is not in the lookup.
  chart_title  <- construct_title(label)
  y_axis_label <- construct_y_label(label)

  # NOTE: `direction` (this function's own parameter) is not used inside the
  # panel itself. The desired-change wording lives in the group figure's caption
  # (see format_legend_line(), called at each figure's own call site). It is left
  # in the function signature so every call site (ITQ x3, HPQ x2, Days Surfing x1)
  # does not need touching. It is a harmless unused parameter.

  ggplot(summary_stats, aes(x = Timepoint, y = Mean, fill = Timepoint)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.6, color = "black") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Mean - 1.96 * SEM, ymax = Mean + 1.96 * SEM), width = 0.15) +
    annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = y_max * 1.1, label = sig_label, size = 4) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("white", "grey40")) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      # Fixed increment when y_breaks_width is supplied (ITQ PTSD/DSO), otherwise
      # ggplot's own automatic breaks. scales::breaks_width() is used fully-qualified
      # rather than adding library(scales), since it is already installed as a
      # dependency of ggplot2.
      breaks = if (!is.null(y_breaks_width)) scales::breaks_width(y_breaks_width) else waiver(),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))
    ) +
    labs(
      # There is no subtitle. The n, p and desired change for each panel live in the
      # group figure's caption (one line per panel, built by format_legend_line() at
      # each figure's own call site), and are not repeated on every panel.
      title = chart_title,
      x     = NULL,
      y     = y_axis_label,
      fill  = NULL
    ) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      # Unbold and centred. There is no plot.subtitle, because the subtitle itself is
      # not used (see labs() above).
      plot.title      = element_text(size = 10, face = "plain", hjust = 0.5),
      # Matched to build_three_tp_panel()'s x-axis treatment (same angle, hjust and
      # size), so the two-timepoint panels' timepoint labels read consistently with the
      # three-timepoint panels' when the two figure types sit near each other.
      axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1, size = 7)
    )
}

# Small helper: computes just the y-axis max (mean + 95% CI) for a pre/post
# pair, without building the full panel. It is needed so the ITQ figure can
# decide a shared gridline increment for PTSD/DSO *before* calling
# build_two_tp_panel() on either of them. This repeats five lines of
# build_two_tp_panel()'s own Step 1/y_max logic rather than refactoring that
# function to return y_max alongside the plot. The duplication is intentional. If
# build_two_tp_panel()'s summary-stats logic changes, this needs updating to
# match.
compute_two_tp_ymax <- function(pre_col, post_col, data) {
  data |>
    select(all_of(c(pre_col, post_col))) |>
    pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "col", values_to = "value") |>
    filter(!is.na(value)) |>
    summarise(Mean = mean(value), SD = sd(value), N = n(), .by = col) |>
    mutate(SEM = SD / sqrt(N)) |>
    summarise(max(Mean + 1.96 * SEM)) |>
    pull()
}

# Builds one figure-legend line per measure for a two-timepoint group,
# via format_legend_line() (see legend-caption-helpers chunk above).
# Direction is pulled from two_tp_lookup and p/N from two_tp_test_summary
# — the same two tables each panel's own build_two_tp_panel() call
# already draws its Direction argument and significance marker from
# respectively, so this stays consistent with what's actually plotted.
two_tp_legend_lines <- function(labels) {
  labels |>
    map_chr(function(lbl) {
      lookup_row <- two_tp_lookup |> filter(Label == lbl)
      test_row   <- two_tp_test_summary |> filter(Measure == lbl)
      format_legend_line(lbl, test_row$P_Value_Bonferroni, test_row$N, lookup_row$Direction)
    })
}
```

## Part 2 — Three-timepoint panel function, post-hoc brackets, and figures by hypothesis group

Bar chart only. Each three-timepoint panel shows mean ± 95% CI at all three timepoints. The omnibus test's p-value, N and `Direction` sit in the figure caption, one line per panel. The figures themselves are built at the end of this Part, once both panel functions exist.

### Post-hoc significance brackets

::: callout-note
**Significance brackets reflect the post-hoc comparisons.** Stars come from the post-hoc pairwise comparisons in `posthoc_summary`, and not from the omnibus test. Script 05 runs post-hoc comparisons only for measures whose omnibus test was significant, so any panel showing a bracket already has a significant omnibus result. The omnibus statistic (chi-sq or F, and p-value) is reported in the group figure's caption (see the Figure legend helpers section, Part 1).

**Brackets.** A three-timepoint measure has three pairwise comparisons (TP1 vs TP4, TP1 vs TP5, TP4 vs TP5), each with its own result. Each significant-omnibus measure therefore gets one bracket per comparison: a line connecting the two bars compared, with `*` or `ns` above it. The two adjacent-bar comparisons sit at one height, and the TP1-vs-TP5 bracket, which spans the other two, sits higher so the brackets do not collide.

**Bonferroni correction.** `posthoc_summary$P_Value_Bonferroni_Numeric` decides `*` vs `ns`. It is corrected within each measure's hypothesis group (Mental health, Wellbeing, Behaviour, Workplace performance), together with that group's other post-hoc comparisons and two-timepoint tests. For the exploratory measure Intention to Leave it is the uncorrected p-value. The 2-week vs 3-month bracket is included in the correction, although that comparison is not hypothesised. The column is numeric, so it avoids the parsing risk of a "\<0.001" string with a space in it.

**No brackets for non-significant omnibus tests.** `posthoc_summary` has no rows for those measures, because stage 5 never ran the comparison. `build_posthoc_brackets()` returns an empty list in that case, so the chart carries no annotation and the reader takes "not significant" from the p-value in the figure caption.
:::

```{r}
#| label: s06-posthoc-bracket-function
# Builds the bracket lines, end-ticks, and */ns text labels for however
# many pairwise post-hoc comparisons a measure has (0 to 3). Returns a
# list of ggplot layers, which can be added to a plot with `+` — ggplot2
# adds every layer in a list in one go, the same as adding them one at a
# time. An empty list adds nothing, which is what happens for a measure
# whose omnibus test wasn't significant (no rows in posthoc_summary).
build_posthoc_brackets <- function(label, posthoc_data, y_max) {

  rows <- posthoc_data |> filter(Measure == label)
  if (nrow(rows) == 0) return(list())

  # TP1/TP4/TP5 map onto this chart's three bar positions in order — matches
  # the fixed factor levels used everywhere else in build_three_tp_panel().
  tp_x <- c(TP1 = 1, TP4 = 2, TP5 = 3)

  rows <- rows |>
    mutate(
      x1        = tp_x[Group1],
      x2        = tp_x[Group2],
      span      = abs(x2 - x1),
      sig_label = if_else(P_Value_Bonferroni_Numeric < 0.05, "*", "ns")
    ) |>
    arrange(span)

  # Two height levels only — with three timepoints, a comparison's span is
  # always either 1 (an adjacent pair) or 2 (TP1 vs TP5, the full range),
  # so two heights are always enough to avoid brackets overlapping.
  bracket_height <- c(`1` = y_max * 1.15, `2` = y_max * 1.35)
  label_offset    <- y_max * 0.05
  tick_length     <- y_max * 0.03

  layers <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(rows))) {
    row   <- rows[i, ]
    y_pos <- bracket_height[[as.character(row$span)]]

    layers <- c(layers, list(
      # The horizontal bracket line itself, plus a short vertical tick at
      # each end so it reads as a bracket rather than a floating line.
      annotate("segment", x = row$x1, xend = row$x2, y = y_pos, yend = y_pos),
      annotate("segment", x = row$x1, xend = row$x1, y = y_pos, yend = y_pos - tick_length),
      annotate("segment", x = row$x2, xend = row$x2, y = y_pos, yend = y_pos - tick_length),
      annotate("text", x = (row$x1 + row$x2) / 2, y = y_pos + label_offset,
               label = row$sig_label, size = 4)
    ))
  }

  layers
}
```

### Reusable panel-building function

```{r}
#| label: s06-three-tp-panel-function
# Same idea as the two-timepoint function above, but reads from
# three_tp_long (already complete-case filtered by stage 5) and
# omnibus_summary (RM-ANOVA or Friedman results) instead. It also takes
# posthoc_summary, to draw significance brackets (see build_posthoc_brackets()
# above). The omnibus result is still reported, in the group figure's caption
# (see three_tp_legend_lines()), but it does not drive the significance marker
# itself.
build_three_tp_panel <- function(label, long_data, direction, omnibus, posthoc) {

  summary_stats <- long_data |>
    summarise(
      Mean = mean(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
      SD   = sd(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
      N    = n(),
      SEM  = SD / sqrt(N),
      .by  = Timepoint
    ) |>
    mutate(Timepoint = factor(Timepoint, levels = c("TP1", "TP4", "TP5"),
                               labels = unname(tp_labels[c("TP1", "TP4", "TP5")])))

  # NOTE: `omnibus` (this function's own parameter) is not used inside the panel
  # itself. The p-value it holds lives in the group figure's caption (built
  # separately at each figure's call site, via three_tp_legend_lines() below,
  # which reads omnibus_summary directly rather than through this function). It
  # is left in the signature so every call site does not need touching. It is a
  # harmless unused parameter.

  y_max <- max(summary_stats$Mean + 1.96 * summary_stats$SEM)

  posthoc_rows   <- posthoc |> filter(Measure == label)
  posthoc_layers <- build_posthoc_brackets(label, posthoc, y_max)

  # Top of the y-axis is set explicitly here, rather than relying on
  # scale_y_continuous()'s automatic expansion alone. That automatic
  # calculation takes its range from the highest thing actually drawn on
  # the panel — once the bracket labels (up near y_max * 1.40 when
  # present) count as part of the data, the expansion percentage was
  # being added on TOP of that already-inflated range, compounding into
  # far more empty space than intended (this is what produced the very
  # tall, mostly-empty panels on first render). limits = c(0, axis_top)
  # below fixes the axis top directly; expand = c(0, 0) then adds no
  # further padding on top of that. This only touches the y scale — the
  # x-axis (Timepoint) keeps its own default padding around the bars,
  # unaffected.
  axis_top <- if (nrow(posthoc_rows) > 0) y_max * 1.45 else y_max * 1.25

  # Same lookup as build_two_tp_panel(): 04c's chart titles and y labels.
  chart_title  <- construct_title(label)
  y_axis_label <- construct_y_label(label)

  ggplot(summary_stats, aes(x = Timepoint, y = Mean, fill = Timepoint)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.6, color = "black") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Mean - 1.96 * SEM, ymax = Mean + 1.96 * SEM), width = 0.15) +
    posthoc_layers +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("white", "grey65", "grey30")) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, axis_top), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
    labs(
      # There is no subtitle. The n, p, desired change and omnibus test information
      # live in the group figure's caption (one line per panel, via
      # three_tp_legend_lines()), and are not repeated on every panel. The omnibus
      # test's name and statistic remain available in omnibus_summary and the
      # exported .xlsx.
      title = chart_title,
      x     = NULL,
      y     = y_axis_label,
      fill  = NULL
    ) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      # Unbold and centred. There is no plot.subtitle, because the subtitle itself is
      # not used (see labs() above).
      plot.title      = element_text(size = 10, face = "plain", hjust = 0.5),
      axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1, size = 7)
    )
}
```

# Builds one figure-legend line per measure for a three-timepoint group, via
# format_legend_line(). Direction is pulled from three_tp_measures and p/N
# from omnibus_summary, the same sources each panel already draws on.
three_tp_legend_lines <- function(labels) {
  labels |>
    map_chr(function(lbl) {
      om_row    <- omnibus_summary |> filter(Measure == lbl)
      direction <- three_tp_measures$Direction[three_tp_measures$Label == lbl]
      format_legend_line(lbl, om_row$P_Value, om_row$N, direction)
    })
}

# One three-timepoint bar-chart panel per label.
make_three_tp_panels <- function(labels) {
  labels |>
    map(function(lbl) {
      direction <- three_tp_measures$Direction[three_tp_measures$Label == lbl]
      build_three_tp_panel(lbl, three_tp_long[[lbl]], direction, omnibus_summary, posthoc_summary)
    })
}

# One two-timepoint bar-chart panel per label.
make_two_tp_panels <- function(labels) {
  labels |>
    map(function(lbl) {
      row <- two_tp_lookup |> filter(Label == lbl)
      build_two_tp_panel(row$PreCol, row$PostCol, lbl, row$Direction, two_tp_data, two_tp_test_summary)
    })
}

## Part 3 — RCI (Reliable Change Index) scatter plots

Scatter plots of TP1 against the follow-up score for each RCI target. The RCI maths and classification are **not** done here. `rci_results` already has each person classified in stage 5, using the same five-category scheme (Recovered / Improved / Unchanged / Deteriorated / Harmed) for every target, ITQ included. This section only builds the percentage labels, colour mapping and the scatter plot itself.

::: callout-note
**Colours.** This section is the one part of stage 6 that is not greyscale. It uses `theme_classic()`. Script 05 classifies each participant into five categories (Recovered, Improved, Unchanged, Deteriorated, Harmed), matching `clinicalsignificance::cs_combined()`. The plot displays three: blue `#4393C3` (Improved), `gray70` (Unchanged) and red `#B2182B` (Deteriorated). Recovered is folded into Improved and Harmed into Deteriorated for display only, because five colours plus the cutoff crosshair made the plot hard to read. Legend labels read "Category (pct%)", and the caption notes that Improved and Deteriorated each include those who also crossed the cutoff.
:::

::: callout-note
**Reliable-change band.** The shaded region around the identity line shows how much change is small enough to be explained by measurement error alone, which is what separates Unchanged from Improved or Deteriorated. Its half-width comes from stage 5's RCI formula. Script 05 does not save `s_diff`, so it is recomputed here from `sd(score_pre)` for this comparison's filtered sample and `Reliability` from `rci_targets`. The band boundary lines up with the points stage 5 classifies as Unchanged.
:::

### Plotting functions

```{r}
#| label: s06-rci-band-function
# Reliable-change band: the shaded region around the diagonal identity
# line within which a change is small enough to be explained by
# measurement error alone. Points inside the band = Unchanged; points
# outside = a reliable change (Improved/Deteriorated, or Recovered/Harmed
# for the four measures that also have a cutoff to cross).
#
# Boundary = identity line +/- 1.96 * s_diff, the same 95% critical value
# used everywhere else in this pipeline's RCI logic (inherited from
# cs_distribution()). s_diff reproduces stage 5's own formula
# (se_measurement = sd_pre * sqrt(1 - reliability); s_diff = sqrt(2) *
# se_measurement), computed here from sd(score_pre) in this already-filtered
# comparison (the same complete-case sample stage 5 used to classify it)
# and the Reliability value carried in rci_targets, so nothing new needs to
# come from stage 5.
#
# x_span is the 2-element c(start, end) the band should cover, supplied by
# the caller so it exactly matches that plot's own axis limits (0 to
# axis_max) and does not only cover the spread of the data points.
# Otherwise the band would stop short of the plot edges wherever the axes
# extend further than the data does. Every call site in this document uses
# matching x and y limits (coord_fixed(xlim = ylim = c(0, axis_max))), so
# x_span also doubles as the valid y-range to clamp the band to.
#
# Returns n_points rows across x_span, with ymin/ymax clamped to x_span's
# own bounds via pmax()/pmin(), and not a raw, unclamped 2-point ribbon. This
# matters: the band's edges (identity line +/- half-width) go below 0 (or
# above axis_max) near the plot's corners, and clip = "off" (used so a point
# sitting exactly at 0 does not have its circle sliced by the panel edge)
# applies to every layer in the plot, not just points. An unclamped band's
# below-zero portion would therefore spill out below the x-axis. Clamping the
# band's own data here means it never has a vertex outside the plot box, so
# clip = "off" does not affect it, while still applying to points as intended.
build_rci_band <- function(df, reliability, x_span, n_points = 100) {

  sd_pre         <- sd(df$score_pre, na.rm = TRUE)
  se_measurement <- sd_pre * sqrt(1 - reliability)
  s_diff         <- sqrt(2) * se_measurement
  half_width     <- 1.96 * s_diff

  x_seq <- seq(x_span[1], x_span[2], length.out = n_points)

  data.frame(
    x    = x_seq,
    ymin = pmax(x_span[1], x_seq - half_width),
    ymax = pmin(x_span[2], x_seq + half_width)
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: s06-rci-plot-functions
# Standard RCI scatter (used for every RCI target, ITQ included). df is one
# entry from rci_results, already with score_pre, score_post, RCI and JT_raw.
# cutoff is optional (NULL for measures with no clinical cutoff, e.g. BRS,
# UWES). reliability is this target's Reliability value from rci_targets,
# needed for the band.
#
# JT_raw holds one of five category strings from stage 5's jt_classify():
# "Recovered", "Improved", "Unchanged", "Deteriorated", "Harmed". For
# DISPLAY here, Recovered is folded into Improved and Harmed into
# Deteriorated, leaving three colours instead of five. Five colours plus the
# cutoff crosshair made the plot too noisy to read at a glance, and the
# cutoff-crossing distinction (Recovered vs plain Improved, Harmed vs plain
# Deteriorated) is explained separately in presentations. This is a
# display-only recode (JT_display, built inside this function).
# rci_results$JT_raw itself, and everything stage 5 computes from it, is
# untouched. The four cutoff-bearing measures still show the cutoff crosshair
# (dashed lines), so a reader who wants to know whether an
# Improved/Deteriorated point also crossed the cutoff can read that directly
# off which quadrant it falls in.
#
# For the twelve measures with no clinical cutoff (MHSIS, BRS, UWES, OSES,
# BAT Total + 4 subscales, and the three ITQ totals), only
# Improved/Unchanged/Deteriorated can appear in the data at all
# (Recovered/Harmed require a cutoff to cross), so the merge has no effect
# there. The legend/colour mapping is built from whichever categories are
# actually present, and not from a fixed list.
plot_rci_standard <- function(df, label, followup_label, cutoff = NULL, reliability, axis_max = NULL) {

  df <- df |>
    mutate(JT_display = case_when(
      JT_raw == "Recovered" ~ "Improved",
      JT_raw == "Harmed"    ~ "Deteriorated",
      TRUE                  ~ JT_raw
    ))

  category_order <- c("Improved", "Unchanged", "Deteriorated")

    # Colours differ in lightness as well as hue, for greyscale printing.
    # Improved and Deteriorated use the same two colours as stage 8's bar charts
    # ("#4393C3" and "#B2182B"); Unchanged is gray70.
  base_colors <- c(
    "Improved"     = "#4393C3",
    "Unchanged"    = "gray70",
    "Deteriorated" = "#B2182B"
  )

  label_df <- df |>
    count(JT_display, name = "n") |>
    mutate(
      pct      = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1),
      JT_label = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", JT_display, pct)
    ) |>
    arrange(match(JT_display, category_order))

  df <- df |>
    left_join(label_df, by = "JT_display") |>
    mutate(JT_label = factor(JT_label, levels = label_df$JT_label))

  color_map <- setNames(base_colors[label_df$JT_display], label_df$JT_label)

  # Axes start at (0, 0) and share a common upper bound — normally the
  # highest observed score (pre or post) in THIS df, or the cutoff if that
  # happens to sit higher, with 5% headroom so the top point isn't flush
  # against the plot edge. If the caller supplies axis_max directly (the
  # standard-targets loop does, using the larger of its TP4 and TP5 data),
  # that value is used instead, so both panels of the same measure share
  # identical axis limits rather than each auto-scaling to its own
  # completers' range. Either way, the band uses this same value, so it
  # reaches exactly to the plot's edges.
  if (is.null(axis_max)) {
    axis_max <- max(c(df$score_pre, df$score_post, cutoff), na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05
  }
  band_df <- build_rci_band(df, reliability, x_span = c(0, axis_max))

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = score_pre, y = score_post)) +
        # Light fill (grey90, alpha 0.35): the band should read as a subtle
        # backdrop and not compete visually with the points sitting on top of it.
    geom_ribbon(data = band_df, aes(x = x, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
                inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey90", alpha = 0.35) +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dotted") +
        # Overplotting is shown via transparency: several measures use narrow
        # integer scales (e.g. GAD-7 0-21), so more than one person can land on the
        # exact same (pre, post) coordinate. alpha = 0.45 means a single point reads
        # as a light dot, but two or more points stacked on the same coordinate
        # compound (each layer's colour shows through the ones below it) into a
        # visibly darker, more saturated dot. No separate size encoding or legend is
        # needed, and no point moves off its true value the way jitter would.
    geom_point(aes(color = JT_label), alpha = 0.45, size = 2.5) +
    scale_color_manual(values = color_map) +
        # expand = FALSE pins (0, 0) exactly into the plot's corner. With expand =
        # FALSE and a hard limit at exactly 0, any point whose true value IS 0 would
        # have its circle sliced in half by the panel edge, since a point's visual
        # radius extends slightly past its coordinate in every direction. clip =
        # "off" lets a point's glyph bleed a couple of pixels past the stated axis
        # limit so the whole circle renders, without moving the axis limits, the
        # band, or the (0, 0) corner. The band's own polygon is already bounded
        # exactly to [0, axis_max], so it does not bleed.
    coord_fixed(xlim = c(0, axis_max), ylim = c(0, axis_max), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
    theme_classic() +
        # Axis and legend text sizes are set slightly above the theme_classic()
        # defaults (base_size = 11) so they read clearly at export size.
        #
        # plot.title is centred to match the bar-chart panels' own centred titles
        # (theme_classic()'s default is left-aligned, hjust = 0). It is left plain,
        # since theme_classic()'s default plot.title is already unbold.
    theme(
      plot.title   = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      axis.text    = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.title   = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.text  = element_text(size = 10),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 12)
    ) +
    labs(
            # Construct title (e.g. "Wellbeing") and not the instrument code, from the
            # same lookup the three-timepoint bar-chart panels use. Which
            # instrument/scale this is stays off the plot; the manuscript's own figure
            # legend supplies it (e.g. "SWEMWBS Metric", "PHQ-8 Total").
      title    = construct_title(label),
            # n sits in the classification legend's own title, as a second line
            # directly beneath "Classification", next to the per-category percentages.
            # There is no subtitle.
      x        = "1-Week Before score",
      y        = paste0(followup_label, " score"),
      color    = paste0("Classification\n(n = ", nrow(df), ")")
    )

  if (!is.null(cutoff)) {
    p <- p +
      geom_vline(xintercept = cutoff, linetype = "dashed") +
      geom_hline(yintercept = cutoff, linetype = "dashed")
  }

  p
}

# The ITQ totals (PTSD, DSO, CPTSD) use plot_rci_standard() above like every
# other target, since their rci_results entries carry the same five-category
# JT_raw scheme as everything else. There is no separate ITQ plotting function.
```

### RCI targets (17 measures: 13 × TP1 vs TP4 and TP1 vs TP5; ITQ PTSD/DSO/CPTSD and HPQ Presenteeism × TP1 vs TP5 only)

```{r}
#| label: fig-rci-standard
#| fig-cap: "RCI scatter plots, all targets"
#| results: asis

# The three DISPLAYED categories, the overplotting encoding, the actual cutoff
# value, and an explanation of the reliable-change band are explained in the
# caption, and not in the legend or as separate on-plot annotations, so each
# exported figure is self-contained and does not depend on a reader having this
# document or a separate methods write-up open alongside it.
#
# wrap_caption() uses base R's strwrap() (no extra package) to break the caption
# into multiple lines at a given character width, so a long caption is not cut
# off at the figure's edge. width = 85 is tuned for the standard RCI figures'
# 7-inch export width (see save_fig() call below); the ITQ figure uses a wider
# value since it exports at 12 inches (see its own plot_annotation() call
# further down).
wrap_caption <- function(text, width = 85) {
  paste(strwrap(text, width = width), collapse = "\n")
}

# format_number() formats both the cutoff value and the reliability value.
format_number <- function(x) {
  if (x == round(x)) as.character(round(x)) else as.character(signif(x, 3))
}

build_rci_caption <- function(cutoff = NULL, reliability = NULL) {

    # What the band is and how it is calculated, in the same terms as stage 5's
    # own s_diff/SEM formula, attributed to its source, Jacobson & Truax (1991).
  band_explanation <- paste(
    "Shaded band = the reliable-change band: the region around the diagonal",
    "within which a change is small enough to be explained by measurement",
    "error alone (not a reliable change), following the Reliable Change",
    "Index (RCI; Jacobson & Truax, 1991). Band width = +/-1.96 x s_diff,",
    "where s_diff = sqrt(2) x SEM and SEM = SD(baseline scores) x",
    "sqrt(1 - reliability)."
  )

  # The specific reliability value actually used for this measure (mostly
  # Cronbach's alpha computed live from TP1 item data; GSPA uses a
  # sourced ICC of 0.74 instead, per stage 5's own callout) — so the
  # caption states not just the formula but the actual number that went
  # into it for this particular figure.
  reliability_note <- if (!is.null(reliability)) {
    sprintf("Reliability used for this measure: %s.", format_number(reliability))
  } else {
    ""
  }

  overplotting_note <- "Points are semi-transparent, so overlapping observations at the same coordinate appear as a darker dot (overplotting)."

  category_note <- if (!is.null(cutoff)) {
    paste(
      "Improved = reliable improvement (including those who also crossed into the functional range).",
      "Unchanged = no reliable change.",
      "Deteriorated = reliable decline (including those who also crossed into the dysfunctional range).",
      sprintf("Dashed lines = published clinical cutoff (%s).", format_number(cutoff))
    )
  } else {
    paste(
      "Improved = reliable improvement.",
      "Unchanged = no reliable change.",
      "Deteriorated = reliable decline."
    )
  }

  exploratory_note <- paste(
    "Exploratory analysis: the RCI is used to show the spread of individual-level",
    "change alongside the group-level results. No threshold for the proportion of",
    "participants improving or deteriorating was set, and no hypothesis is tested."
  )

  wrap_caption(paste(exploratory_note, band_explanation, reliability_note, overplotting_note, category_note))
}

rci_standard_plots <- list()

# Captures each ITQ target's bare TP1-vs-TP5 panel (p_tp5, no caption
# attached) as it is built inside the loop below, so a combined three-panel ITQ
# figure can be assembled afterwards without re-running plot_rci_standard() a
# second time. HPQ Presenteeism (stage 5) also has no TP4 comparison and hits
# the same has_tp4 == FALSE branch this list is built in, but it does NOT go in
# here, since it has its own separate figure and is not part of the three-panel
# ITQ group. See the explicit label check inside the loop below.
itq_rci_panels <- list()

# Height each measure's combined figure needs when exported, tracked alongside
# the plot itself. Standard targets have both a TP4 and TP5 panel stacked
# (nrow = 2), needing more vertical space than the ITQ targets, which only have a
# TP5 panel (ITQ is not administered at TP4, so there is no TP1-vs-TP4
# comparison to plot). Used by the export loop below instead of one fixed height
# for every measure.
rci_plot_heights <- c()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(rci_targets))) {

  label   <- rci_targets$Label[i]
  cutoff  <- if (is.na(rci_targets$Cutoff[i])) NULL else rci_targets$Cutoff[i]
  has_tp4 <- !is.na(rci_targets$TP4Col[i])

  key_tp5 <- paste0(label, "__TP1_vs_TP5")
  reliability <- rci_targets$Reliability[i]
  df_tp5 <- rci_results[[key_tp5]]

  if (has_tp4) {

    key_tp4 <- paste0(label, "__TP1_vs_TP4")
    df_tp4  <- rci_results[[key_tp4]]

        # Shared axis_max across both panels of this measure. Otherwise TP4 and TP5
        # each auto-scale to their own completers' range, which can differ slightly
        # (different N at each follow-up), making the two panels harder to compare
        # directly even though they sit side by side in the same figure.
    axis_max <- max(c(df_tp4$score_pre, df_tp4$score_post,
                       df_tp5$score_pre, df_tp5$score_post, cutoff), na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05

    p_tp4 <- plot_rci_standard(df_tp4, label, unname(tp_labels[["TP4"]]), cutoff, reliability, axis_max)
    p_tp5 <- plot_rci_standard(df_tp5, label, unname(tp_labels[["TP5"]]), cutoff, reliability, axis_max)

    this_caption <- build_rci_caption(cutoff, reliability)

    combined <- p_tp4 + p_tp5 + plot_layout(nrow = 2) +
      plot_annotation(caption = this_caption) &
      theme(plot.caption = element_text(size = 7, hjust = 0))

    rci_plot_heights[label] <- 12

  } else {

        # ITQ PTSD/DSO/CPTSD and HPQ Presenteeism (stage 5): TP1 vs TP5 only, since
        # neither is administered at TP4. Single-panel figure instead of the usual
        # stacked TP4/TP5 pair. plot_rci_standard() and build_rci_caption() are
        # otherwise identical calls to the has_tp4 branch above.
    axis_max <- max(c(df_tp5$score_pre, df_tp5$score_post, cutoff), na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05

    p_tp5 <- plot_rci_standard(df_tp5, label, unname(tp_labels[["TP5"]]), cutoff, reliability, axis_max)

        # Stashed here, before the caption gets attached below, only for the three ITQ
        # targets. The combined ITQ panel (built after this loop) uses these bare
        # plots with no caption of their own. HPQ Presenteeism gets its own
        # individually captioned figure below like every other RCI target, so it is
        # excluded from this list via the explicit label check and not by
        # has_tp4 == FALSE alone.
    if (label %in% c("ITQ PTSD", "ITQ DSO", "ITQ CPTSD")) {
      itq_rci_panels[[label]] <- p_tp5
    }

    this_caption <- build_rci_caption(cutoff, reliability)

    combined <- p_tp5 +
      plot_annotation(caption = this_caption) &
      theme(plot.caption = element_text(size = 7, hjust = 0))

    rci_plot_heights[label] <- 7
  }

  rci_standard_plots[[label]] <- combined

  print(combined)
}

# Combined three-panel ITQ RCI figure: 2 panels above, 1 below (three across was
# too cramped once each panel carries its own Classification legend).
# itq_rci_panels is ordered PTSD, DSO, CPTSD; with ncol = 2, wrap_plots() fills
# left-to-right, top-to-bottom, so PTSD and DSO land on the top row and CPTSD
# sits alone on the row below. To put a different measure on its own, change
# the panel order.
# No caption is added here, because the figure legend is written by hand, so
# plot_annotation() is deliberately omitted (unlike every other combined RCI
# figure in this document, which all get a caption via build_rci_caption()).
itq_rci_group <- wrap_plots(
  itq_rci_panels[c("ITQ PTSD", "ITQ DSO", "ITQ CPTSD")],
  ncol = 2
)

itq_rci_group
```

## Part 4 — INTL scatter (not RCI)

INTL is deliberately excluded from RCI (stage 5's decision — a 2-item, self-made, unvalidated measure doesn't support a trustworthy reliability estimate). This is a plain scatter instead: 1-Week Before on the x-axis, both follow-up timepoints plotted against it in two shades of grey.

```{r}
#| label: fig-intl-scatter
#| fig-cap: "Intention to Leave: 1-Week Before vs both follow-up timepoints"

intl_data <- scored_data |>
  select(ID, INTL_Total_TP1, INTL_Total_TP4, INTL_Total_TP5) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(INTL_Total_TP4, INTL_Total_TP5),
    names_to  = "Timepoint",
    values_to = "Follow_Up_Score"
  ) |>
  mutate(Timepoint = case_when(
    Timepoint == "INTL_Total_TP4" ~ unname(tp_labels["TP4"]),
    Timepoint == "INTL_Total_TP5" ~ unname(tp_labels["TP5"])
  )) |>
  mutate(Timepoint = factor(Timepoint, levels = unname(tp_labels[c("TP4", "TP5")]))) |>
  filter(!is.na(INTL_Total_TP1), !is.na(Follow_Up_Score))

intl_plot <- ggplot(intl_data, aes(x = INTL_Total_TP1, y = Follow_Up_Score,
                                    color = Timepoint, shape = Timepoint)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.75, size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("grey65", "grey20")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17)) +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    title    = construct_title("INTL Total"),
    subtitle = "Plain scatter, not RCI-classified",
    x        = paste0(unname(tp_labels["TP1"]), " score"),
    y        = "Follow-up score",
    color    = "Follow-up timepoint",
    shape    = "Follow-up timepoint",
    caption  = wrap_caption(paste(
      "Exploratory figure: Intention to Leave is a measure developed by the",
      "authors to test programme theory, and is not part of the RCI analysis.",
      "Points on the dotted line show no change."
    ), width = 90)
  ) +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(size = 7, hjust = 0))

intl_plot
```

## Part 4b — HPQ Absenteeism scatter (not RCI)

HPQ Absenteeism is deliberately excluded from RCI, on the same grounds as INTL above — stage 5's search of the published literature found no defensible reliability estimate for the HPQ absenteeism-hours item in a population close to this study's own (see stage 5's own callout for the full reasoning and sources checked). Same treatment as the INTL scatter: 1-Week Before on the x-axis, the follow-up timepoint on the y-axis. Only one follow-up point here, not two — HPQ isn't administered at TP4, so there's no 2-Week Follow-Up value to plot alongside 3-Month Follow-Up the way INTL has.

```{r}
#| label: fig-hpq-absenteeism-scatter
#| fig-cap: "HPQ Absenteeism: 1-Week Before vs 3-Month Follow-Up"

hpq_absenteeism_data <- scored_data |>
  select(ID, HPQ_absenteeism_hours_4w_TP1, HPQ_absenteeism_hours_4w_TP5) |>
  filter(!is.na(HPQ_absenteeism_hours_4w_TP1), !is.na(HPQ_absenteeism_hours_4w_TP5))

# Four-quadrant version. Absenteeism hours include negative values,
# so the axes cannot start at 0 the way the RCI plots do. One shared range
# is used for both axes (with a small margin) so coord_fixed() keeps the
# dotted "no change" line at a true 45 degrees. The x = 0 and y = 0 lines
# are drawn as reference lines through the middle of the plot, and the
# normal axis lines are removed in favour of a plain box around the panel.
hpq_absenteeism_all <- c(hpq_absenteeism_data$HPQ_absenteeism_hours_4w_TP1,
                         hpq_absenteeism_data$HPQ_absenteeism_hours_4w_TP5)
hpq_absenteeism_pad <- 0.05 * diff(range(hpq_absenteeism_all))
hpq_absenteeism_lim <- c(min(hpq_absenteeism_all) - hpq_absenteeism_pad,
                         max(hpq_absenteeism_all) + hpq_absenteeism_pad)

hpq_absenteeism_plot <- ggplot(
  hpq_absenteeism_data,
  aes(x = HPQ_absenteeism_hours_4w_TP1, y = HPQ_absenteeism_hours_4w_TP5)
) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.75, size = 2, color = "grey20", shape = 17) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = hpq_absenteeism_lim, ylim = hpq_absenteeism_lim, expand = FALSE) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.line    = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 7, hjust = 0)
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = construct_title("HPQ Absenteeism Hours (4w)"),
    subtitle = "Plain scatter, not RCI-classified",
    x        = paste0(unname(tp_labels["TP1"]), " \u2014 ", construct_y_label("HPQ Absenteeism Hours (4w)")),
    y        = paste0(unname(tp_labels["TP5"]), " \u2014 ", construct_y_label("HPQ Absenteeism Hours (4w)")),
    caption  = wrap_caption(paste(
      "Exploratory figure: absenteeism is not part of the RCI analysis, and no",
      "hypothesis is tested here. Points on the dotted line show no change,",
      "points below it show fewer hours at follow-up. Negative values are plotted",
      "as recorded. Semi-transparent points darken where observations overlap."
    ), width = 90)
  )

hpq_absenteeism_plot
```

## Export all figures

```{r}
#| label: s06-export-figures
if (!dir.exists(here("data", "analysis"))) {
  dir.create(here("data", "analysis"), recursive = TRUE)
}

save_fig <- function(plot, filename, width = 10, height = 8) {
  ggsave(
    filename = here("data", "analysis", filename),
    plot     = plot,
    width    = width,
    height   = height,
    units    = "in",
    dpi      = 300,
    bg       = "white"
  )
}

# Bar-chart figures, one file per figure, grouped by hypothesis group.
save_fig(mental_health_figure,      "fig_mental_health.png",                 width = 10, height = 9)
save_fig(wellbeing_plot,            "fig_wellbeing.png",                     width = 5,  height = 5)
save_fig(behaviour_figure,          "fig_behaviour.png",                     width = 8,  height = 5)
save_fig(days_surfing_plot,         "fig_exploratory_days_surfing.png",      width = 4,  height = 4)
save_fig(burnout_figure,            "fig_workplace_burnout.png",             width = 12, height = 8)
save_fig(work_performance_figure,   "fig_workplace_work_performance.png",    width = 7,  height = 4)
save_fig(other_occupational_figure, "fig_workplace_other.png",               width = 8,  height = 8)

# RCI targets — one combined file per measure. Height varies: 12in for
# measures with both a TP4 and TP5 panel stacked, 7in for the three ITQ
# targets (TP1 vs TP5 only, single panel) — see rci_plot_heights, built
# alongside rci_standard_plots above.
iwalk(rci_standard_plots, function(plot, label) {
  safe_name <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", label)
  save_fig(plot, paste0("fig_rci_", safe_name, ".png"), width = 7, height = rci_plot_heights[[label]])
})

# Combined three-panel ITQ RCI figure, with no caption (the figure legend is
# written by hand). Width/height are estimated for the 2-above-1-below layout:
# individual panels export square-ish at 7x7in each, so two side by side on the
# top row suggests ~14in wide, and two stacked rows suggests ~14in tall. This
# is an estimate, not measured against a render.
save_fig(itq_rci_group, "fig_rci_itq_group.png", width = 14, height = 14)

# INTL scatter
save_fig(intl_plot, "fig_intl_scatter.png", width = 6, height = 6)

# HPQ Absenteeism scatter
save_fig(hpq_absenteeism_plot, "fig_hpq_absenteeism_scatter.png", width = 6, height = 6)

message("All figures saved to data/analysis/")
```

# Stage 7: Programme theory figure

## How this stage runs

**Reads:** `data/clean/program_theory.xlsx` (written by stage 2).

**Writes:** `data/analysis/fig_progtheory_choices_TP4.png`.

This stage visualises `ProgTheory_choice2_TP4`, the multi-select "which of these would you choose" question asked at 2-Week Follow-Up, with an unlimited number of options selectable. It counts how many respondents chose each option and plots the counts as a bar chart.

It is a standalone stage. `ProgTheory_choice2_TP4` is not in stage 5's `.rdata` handoff, because stage 2 extracted it from the main dataset and saved it only to `program_theory.xlsx`, so this stage reads that file directly.

::: callout-warning
**"Other" responses are not folded in.** Stage 2's fold-text step looks for a `_choice1_` column to pair with `_other2_`, but this question is named `ProgTheory_choice2_TP4`, so the automatic pairing does not find it. The Programme Theory columns are also extracted from `merged_data` before the fold step runs, so the fold would not reach them in any case. Anyone who selected "Other" therefore has the literal word `"Other"` in their `ProgTheory_choice2_TP4` value, and their write-in sits unused in `ProgTheory_other2_TP4` (also in the xlsx). This stage counts "Other" as its own bar, which reflects what the data currently contains. Fixing it would mean matching the `choice1`/`choice2` naming and running the fold before extraction in stage 2.
:::

### Setup

```{r}
#| label: s07-setup
#| message: false

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(forcats)
library(ggplot2)
library(readxl)
library(here)
```

### Load and inspect

```{r}
#| label: s07-load-data
program_theory_df <- read_excel(here("data", "clean", "program_theory.xlsx"))

glimpse(program_theory_df)
```

### Split the multi-select responses

Each response is a single comma-separated string (e.g. `"Other mental health services outside of my organisation,Surfwell / Surf Therapy, No preference"`). This step splits each person's string into separate chosen options, one row per person per option — the standard way to turn a "select all that apply" column into something summarisable. Whitespace is trimmed after splitting since the comma-spacing in the raw data isn't consistent (some commas have a following space, some don't) — without trimming, `"No preference"` and `" No preference"` would be counted as two different options.

```{r}
#| label: s07-split-multiselect
progtheory_choices <- program_theory_df |>
  select(ID, ProgTheory_choice2_TP4) |>
  filter(!is.na(ProgTheory_choice2_TP4), ProgTheory_choice2_TP4 != "") |>
  mutate(Choice = str_split(ProgTheory_choice2_TP4, ",")) |>
  unnest(Choice) |>
  mutate(Choice = str_trim(Choice))

n_respondents <- n_distinct(progtheory_choices$ID)

message("Respondents who answered this question: ", n_respondents)
```

### Count how many people chose each option

Percentages are calculated against the number of *respondents* (people who answered the question at all), not the number of *choices* made — since this is a "select all that apply" question, percentages can add up to more than 100%. That's expected here, not an error.

```{r}
#| label: s07-count-choices
choice_summary <- progtheory_choices |>
  count(Choice, name = "N_Chosen") |>
  mutate(
    Percent = round(100 * N_Chosen / n_respondents, 1),
    Choice  = fct_reorder(Choice, N_Chosen)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(N_Chosen))

print(choice_summary)
```

### Bar chart

Horizontal bars, not vertical — several of these option labels are long sentences, and a horizontal layout keeps them readable without rotating or truncating the text.

```{r}
#| label: fig-progtheory-choices
#| fig-cap: "Programme preference (TP4): how many respondents chose each option"

progtheory_plot <- ggplot(choice_summary, aes(x = Choice, y = N_Chosen)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "grey40", color = "black", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(N_Chosen, " (", Percent, "%)")), hjust = -0.1, size = 3.2) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))) +
  labs(
    title   = "Programme Preference — 2-Week Follow-Up",
    x       = NULL,
    y       = "Number of respondents",
        # n sits in the caption and not on the chart itself, matching the other
        # figures in this pipeline. The multi-select explanatory note sits with it,
        # since it reads naturally alongside n.
    caption = paste0("n = ", n_respondents, " respondents. Multi-select question — percentages may sum to more than 100%.")
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
        # Centred, matching the bar-chart panels elsewhere in this pipeline
        # (theme_classic()'s default is left-aligned). It is left plain, since
        # theme_classic()'s default title is already unbold.
    plot.title   = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 7)
  )

progtheory_plot
```

### Export

```{r}
#| label: s07-export-figure
if (!dir.exists(here("data", "analysis"))) {
  dir.create(here("data", "analysis"), recursive = TRUE)
}

ggsave(
  filename = here("data", "analysis", "fig_progtheory_choices_TP4.png"),
  plot     = progtheory_plot,
  width    = 9,
  height   = 5,
  units    = "in",
  dpi      = 300,
  bg       = "white"
)

message("Saved: data/analysis/fig_progtheory_choices_TP4.png")
```

# Stage 8: RCI stacked-bar figures

## How this stage runs

**Reads:** `data/analysis/analysis_results.rdata` (stage 5) and `data/analysis/measure_groups.rdata` (stage 4c).

**Writes:** the stacked-bar figures, to `data/analysis/`.

This stage draws the RCI classifications from stage 5 as 100%-stacked bar charts, one bar per construct, showing the percentage of participants who improved, did not change or deteriorated. There is one figure per comparison (1-Week Before vs 2-Week Follow-Up, and 1-Week Before vs 3-Month Follow-Up). The bars are split into one panel per hypothesis group (Mental health, Wellbeing, Behaviour, Workplace performance), read from the lookup made by stage 4c, and each panel has a bracket above its bars with the group name. The x axis shows the construct with the instrument in brackets (for example "Depression Symptoms (PHQ-8)"). The participant count and other notes are in the figure caption.

**Exploratory.** The RCI is used to show the spread of individual-level change alongside the group-level results. No hypothesis is tested. Intention to Leave and HPQ Absenteeism are not in the RCI, so they do not appear.

### Setup

```{r}
#| label: s08-setup
#| message: false

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(here)

load(here("data", "analysis", "analysis_results.rdata"))
load(here("data", "analysis", "measure_groups.rdata"))

if (!exists("measure_family") || !exists("family_order")) {
  stop("measure_groups.rdata is missing measure_family or family_order. ",
       "Run stage 4c first.", call. = FALSE)
}
```

### Which measures go in each figure

```{r}
#| label: s08-measure-lists
# TP1 vs TP4: only measures with a TP4 comparison. ITQ has TP4Col = NA (not
# collected at 2-Week Follow-Up), so it drops out here automatically.
measures_tp4 <- rci_targets$Label[!is.na(rci_targets$TP4Col)]

# TP1 vs TP5: every RCI target.
measures_tp5 <- rci_targets$Label
```

### Building the data

::: callout-note
**Five RCI categories become four.** `jt_classify()` in stage 5 gives Recovered, Improved, Unchanged, Deteriorated or Harmed. Recovered counts as Improve and Harmed counts as Deteriorate. Anyone missing a score for a measure counts as N/A, so every bar has the same total (everyone RCI-eligible on at least one measure in that figure), and the grey segment shows how much data is missing for that construct.
:::

```{r}
#| label: s08-rci-grid-function
# One row per participant per measure, with the four-category classification.
build_rci_grid <- function(measure_labels, comparison_suffix) {

  per_measure <- map_dfr(measure_labels, function(lbl) {
    df <- rci_results[[paste0(lbl, comparison_suffix)]]
    if (is.null(df)) return(NULL)
    df |> select(id, JT_raw) |> mutate(Measure = lbl)
  })

  expand_grid(id = sort(unique(per_measure$id)), Measure = measure_labels) |>
    left_join(per_measure, by = c("id", "Measure")) |>
    mutate(
      Category = case_when(
        is.na(JT_raw)                             ~ "N/A",
        str_detect(JT_raw, "^Recovered|^Improv")  ~ "Improve",
        str_detect(JT_raw, "^Unchanged")          ~ "No Change",
        str_detect(JT_raw, "^Harmed|^Deteriorat") ~ "Deteriorate",
        TRUE                                      ~ "N/A"
      ),
      Category = factor(Category, levels = c("Improve", "No Change", "Deteriorate", "N/A"))
    )
}
```

### Axis labels and group order

```{r}
#| label: s08-axis-labels
# Instrument name as it should be printed in brackets. BAT is written BAT-12;
# the ITQ and HPQ sub-measures show just the instrument.
instrument_name <- function(label) {
  case_when(
    str_detect(label, "^BAT") ~ "BAT-12",
    str_detect(label, "^ITQ") ~ "ITQ",
    str_detect(label, "^HPQ") ~ "HPQ",
    TRUE                      ~ label
  )
}

# Construct name for the axis: the chart title from the lookup, with the
# "Burnout: " prefix removed from the BAT sub-scales (so they read
# "Exhaustion", not "Burnout: Exhaustion"). The construct is on one line
# and the instrument on a second line; the labels are drawn vertically
# (see the plot functions), so they cannot overlap neighbouring bars.
axis_label <- function(label, wrap_width = 100) {
  construct <- map_chr(label, measure_text, what = "chart_title") |>
    str_remove("^Burnout: ")
  paste0(str_wrap(construct, width = wrap_width), "\n(", instrument_name(label), ")")
}

# Attaches family (group), order and axis label to the grid. Order is:
# family in the order used elsewhere, then the sub-group and display order
# from the lookup. Every measure in the figure must have a family; the
# exploratory measures (no family) are not RCI targets, so none is expected.
add_axis_info <- function(grid, measure_labels) {
  info <- tibble(Measure = measure_labels) |>
    add_measure_groups("Measure") |>
    mutate(Family = measure_family(Measure))

  if (anyNA(info$Family)) {
    stop("RCI measure(s) with no hypothesis group: ",
         paste(info$Measure[is.na(info$Family)], collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }

  info <- info |>
    mutate(Family = factor(Family, levels = family_order)) |>
    arrange(Family, sub_group, display_order) |>
    mutate(Axis = axis_label(Measure))

  grid |>
    left_join(select(info, Measure, Family, SubGroup = sub_group, Axis), by = "Measure") |>
    mutate(Axis = factor(Axis, levels = info$Axis))
}
```

### Plot functions

```{r}
#| label: s08-plot-functions
# Chosen so the four categories stay distinguishable when printed in
# greyscale: they step evenly in lightness (grey levels about 72, 129, 191
# and 242, darkest to lightest), not only in hue. Improve and Deteriorate
# keep a blue/red pairing from ColorBrewer's RdBu palette. The same two
# colours are used in stage 6's RCI scatter plots.
rci_colours <- c(
  "Deteriorate" = "#B2182B",
  "Improve"     = "#4393C3",
  "N/A"         = "#BFBFBF",
  "No Change"   = "#F2F2F2"
)[c("Improve", "No Change", "Deteriorate", "N/A")]

pct_labels <- function(x) paste0(round(x * 100), "%")

# Wraps caption text to a fixed line width so it does not run off the figure.
wrap_caption <- function(text, width = 110) paste(strwrap(text, width = width), collapse = "\n")

# One panel per hypothesis group. space = "free_x" makes each panel as wide
# as its number of bars, so all bars are the same width. The usual panel
# headers are switched off and replaced by a bracket above each panel's
# bars with the group name. The bracket data is built from the grid, so it
# follows whichever measures are in the figure.
plot_rci_bars_panels <- function(grid, title, caption) {
  axis_tbl <- grid |>
    distinct(Family, SubGroup, Axis) |>
    arrange(Axis) |>
    mutate(idx = row_number(), .by = Family)

  family_tbl <- axis_tbl |>
    summarise(xmin = min(idx) - 0.4, xmax = max(idx) + 0.4,
              xmid = mean(range(idx)), .by = Family) |>
    mutate(label = str_wrap(as.character(Family), width = 12))

  ggplot(grid, aes(x = Axis, fill = Category)) +
    geom_bar(position = "fill", color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    # Bracket and name for each hypothesis group
    geom_segment(data = family_tbl, aes(x = xmin, xend = xmax, y = 1.03, yend = 1.03),
                 inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_text(data = family_tbl, aes(x = xmid, y = 1.045, label = label),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, fontface = "bold", vjust = 0, size = 3.5, lineheight = 0.9) +
    facet_grid(. ~ Family, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = rci_colours, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_labels, breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1), clip = "off") +
    labs(title = title, caption = caption, x = NULL,
         y = "% of participants", fill = "RCI Classification") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
      panel.grid      = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing.x = unit(1.2, "lines"),
      strip.text      = element_blank(),
      # Extra space under the title for the brackets and their names
      plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 40)),
      plot.caption    = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9),
      plot.margin     = margin(t = 8, r = 8, b = 8, l = 8)
    )
}
```

# Stage 9: Package citations and reproducibility record

## How this stage runs

**Reads:** this document itself (`surfwell_study2_pipeline.qmd`), as plain text. Nothing is executed and no study data is touched.

**Writes:** `data/analysis/pipeline_citations.bib` (one BibTeX entry for R and one per package, importable into EndNote) and `data/analysis/pipeline_sessionInfo.txt` (the R version and the version of every package loaded in the current session, for a methods or reproducibility appendix).

What it does:

1.  Finds the pipeline file and reads the code chunks only, skipping prose and comment lines.
2.  Collects every package named in a `library()` or `require()` call, and every package used through a `package::function()` call without being loaded.
3.  Removes duplicates and the packages that come with base R, which the citation for R itself covers.
4.  Asks R for each package's citation, and reports any package that is not installed.
5.  Writes the `.bib` file and checks it for duplicate entry keys.
6.  Saves the session information.

::: callout-warning
**This records the packages installed in the current R session.** `citation()` and `sessionInfo()` read the live R environment, so they report the package versions you have now, and these may differ from the versions used when the results were produced. For a trustworthy version record, run stages 1 to 8 in one session, then run this stage in that same session. `sessionInfo()` lists only packages loaded at that moment.
:::

### Setup

```{r}
#| label: s09-setup
#| message: false

library(here)
library(stringr)
library(purrr)
library(dplyr)
```

### Step 1: Read the code chunks of the pipeline file

This finds `surfwell_study2_pipeline.qmd` and keeps only the lines inside `{r}` code chunks that are not comments. If the file is saved somewhere other than the project root, change `pipeline_file` to its path.

```{r}
#| label: s09-read-code

pipeline_file <- here("surfwell_study2_pipeline.qmd")

if (!file.exists(pipeline_file)) {
  stop("Cannot find ", pipeline_file, ". Edit `pipeline_file` above to point at the pipeline .qmd.",
       call. = FALSE)
}

pipeline_lines <- readLines(pipeline_file, warn = FALSE)

# Track whether each line sits inside an {r} chunk. A chunk opens with ```{r
# and closes at the next line that starts with ```. Other fenced blocks in the
# prose (such as the example in the introduction) are ignored.
in_chunk <- logical(length(pipeline_lines))
inside <- FALSE

for (i in seq_along(pipeline_lines)) {
  line <- pipeline_lines[i]
  if (!inside && str_detect(line, "^```\\{r")) {
    inside <- TRUE
  } else if (inside && str_detect(line, "^```")) {
    inside <- FALSE
  } else {
    in_chunk[i] <- inside
  }
}

code_lines <- pipeline_lines[in_chunk]

# Drop comment-only lines, so a package named in a comment is not counted
code_lines <- code_lines[!str_detect(code_lines, "^\\s*#")]

length(code_lines)
```

### Step 2: Find the packages used

Two patterns are searched for. `library(name)` and `require(name)` catch packages loaded at the top of each stage. `name::` catches packages used without being loaded, such as `scales::breaks_width()`. Both are needed for a complete citation list.

```{r}
#| label: s09-find-packages

loaded_pkgs <- str_extract_all(
  code_lines,
  "(?:library|require)\\(([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9.]*)\\)"
) |>
  unlist() |>
  str_remove_all("^(library|require)\\(|\\)$")

namespace_pkgs <- str_extract_all(
  code_lines,
  "\\b[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9.]*(?=::)"
) |>
  unlist()

# Packages that ship with R. The citation for R itself covers them.
base_pkgs <- c("base", "stats", "utils", "graphics", "grDevices",
               "methods", "tools", "datasets", "grid", "stats4")

packages_long <- bind_rows(
  tibble(Package = loaded_pkgs,    How_used = "library call"),
  tibble(Package = namespace_pkgs, How_used = "double colon call")
) |>
  filter(!Package %in% base_pkgs)

# One row per package, showing every way it was used
unique_packages_tbl <- packages_long |>
  summarise(How_used = paste(sort(unique(How_used)), collapse = " and "),
            .by = Package) |>
  arrange(Package)

unique_packages <- unique_packages_tbl$Package

unique_packages_tbl
```

::: callout-note
**Check this list before moving on.** It is the exact set of packages that will get a BibTeX entry. If a package you expected is missing, or something unexpected appears, fix it here and not after the `.bib` file is written.
:::

### Step 3: Get each citation

`citation("packagename")` returns the citation the package's authors ask for. It is wrapped in `tryCatch()` because it errors for a package that is not installed. A failure is reported and skipped and does not stop the stage. `citation()` with no argument gives the citation for R itself.

```{r}
#| label: s09-generate-citations

get_citation_safe <- function(pkg) {
  tryCatch(
    citation(pkg),
    error = function(e) {
      message("Could not get citation for: ", pkg, " (", conditionMessage(e), ")")
      NULL
    }
  )
}

package_citations <- map(unique_packages, get_citation_safe)
names(package_citations) <- unique_packages

r_citation <- citation()

failed_packages <- unique_packages[map_lgl(package_citations, is.null)]

if (length(failed_packages) > 0) {
  message("Citation lookup failed for: ", paste(failed_packages, collapse = ", "),
          ". These are not installed in this R session. Install them, then re-run this chunk.")
} else {
  message("Citation found for all ", length(unique_packages), " packages.")
}
```

### Step 4: Write the BibTeX file

`toBibtex()` converts each citation into BibTeX text. The file can be imported into EndNote through File, Import, with the BibTeX filter. The chunk also checks that no two entries share a key. EndNote uses the key as the entry's identifier, and duplicate keys can make one entry overwrite another on import.

```{r}
#| label: s09-write-bibtex

if (!dir.exists(here("data", "analysis"))) {
  dir.create(here("data", "analysis"), recursive = TRUE)
}

bib_path <- here("data", "analysis", "pipeline_citations.bib")

successful_citations <- package_citations[!map_lgl(package_citations, is.null)]

all_bibtex <- map(successful_citations, toBibtex) |> unlist()
r_bibtex   <- toBibtex(r_citation)

bib_text <- c(r_bibtex, "", all_bibtex)

writeLines(bib_text, bib_path)

# Entry keys look like "@Manual{R-dplyr," so pull out the text between { and ,
bib_keys <- str_match(bib_text, "^@[A-Za-z]+\\{([^,]+),")[, 2]
bib_keys <- bib_keys[!is.na(bib_keys)]
duplicate_keys <- unique(bib_keys[duplicated(bib_keys)])

if (length(duplicate_keys) > 0) {
  message("Duplicate BibTeX keys: ", paste(duplicate_keys, collapse = ", "),
          ". Edit the .bib file so each key is unique before importing.")
} else {
  message("All BibTeX keys are unique.")
}

message("Saved: ", bib_path, " (", length(successful_citations) + 1, " entries: R + ",
        length(successful_citations), " packages)")
```

### Step 5: Save the session information

This is the version record and not a citation, so it goes in its own plain-text file. It holds the R version, the operating system and the version of every package loaded in the current session.

```{r}
#| label: s09-save-sessioninfo

session_path <- here("data", "analysis", "pipeline_sessionInfo.txt")

writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), session_path)

message("Saved: ", session_path)
```
